skill.title: Directory file discovery skips valid files due to path-form mismatch in extension or ignore filtering
knowledge: Reproduce the discovery through its public directory entry point on a controlled directory containing only one matching-extension file, and observe whether the result is empty, incomplete, or includes wrong files.
Trace the public discovery entry into its low-level helpers for traversal, exact-path handling, extension matching, and ignore-spec loading rather than assuming the bug is in traversal logic.

Use the first observable divergence from expected behavior to identify which filtering layer rejects the file, then compare the path representation entering that layer to the documented or intended one.
Inspect extension predicates for subtle path-form assumptions: a leading ./ prefix, absolute-versus-relative mismatch, or OS-specific separator can make every valid extension test fail.

If ignore patterns seem to suppress valid files, verify whether the ignore matcher receives absolute, relative, or normalized paths and confirm that all call sites use the same path form as the ignore-spec loader.

Directly invoke the suspected helper predicates with controlled inputs to determine which one returns false and what path form it actually expects; this avoids debugging the whole discovery pipeline at once.
skill.trigger: Use when directory traversal or file discovery returns an empty or unexpected file set, or when extension matching / ignore-file processing stops finding expected files after refactoring.

skill.title: Method accesses state-dict keys it never initializes because an internal rewrite helper is defined but not called
knowledge: Read the failing method's body as the owner of the state dict: look for any read of a key like state['x'] before any write to that key.

When a method defines an inner helper or embeds a block of code for a transformation but never calls it, suspect that the missing call is why later state keys are never populated. Search for references to the helper's name or to the output keys to confirm the intended call site.

Do not initialize only the missing key if later code in the method or consumers depends on several derived keys; repair the whole intended transformation sequence (e.g., populate eval_code and memorize_code alongside the state entry).
Use existing in-repo contract tests that inspect the resulting state dict to determine what keys the method is supposed to set, rather than inferring the contract only from the failure site.

Trace callers that pass state={} to understand that no other component can pre-populate the dict; if only the method under inspection touches the dict, the bug is localized there even when the exception mentions a key.

If the method has leftover comments explaining what the missing block should do (for example 'rewrite stateful transforms before memory passes'), treat those comments as the specification and look for a helper that still exists but is orphaned.
Compare the failing path to adjacent methods that consume the dict: when the consumer is unchanged, the fault is in the producer that was supposed to prepare shared state before the consumer runs.
skill.trigger: Use when an API method receives a fresh/previously empty state dict and fails with KeyError, AttributeError, or UnboundLocalError when later consumers expect transformed keys or code to be prepopulated. Also use when the same method contains comments or nested helper definitions about rewriting/transforming state before a phase that never seems to run.

fault_subtype: state-dict uninitialized by its owning method

skill.title: Paired Enable/Disable or Start/Stop Setters Write the Same Boolean Value
knowledge: Locate the class containing the paired setters and read enough source to display both methods side by side; the defect is visible when the disable/stop method assigns the same boolean value as the enable/start method.

Compare the setters field by field rather than reading only one: enable/start should write True and branch on the active run state (running AND periodic is the usual stop opportunity), while disable/stop should write False and branch on the same conjunction, not on not-running OR not-periodic.

Use the method docstring as a hypothesis clue: a severe mismatch between the documented effect and the actual assignment in the method body strengthens that method as the fault candidate before ranking downstream consumers.

After seeing one writer suspect, search the module for every read of the shared state key and list each reader and writer; a reader that filters on the state key is a correct consumer, not the root cause, if the only suspicious writer leaves the key true.

Read the periodic-task launcher and stopper to ground the symptoms: when a start routine launches periodically without rechecking the state key, a stale true value causes sending after disable; verify that the stop helper is only reachable under the same running-and-periodic condition that the buggy setter inverted.

If a callback dispatcher filters messages based on the same state key, the reported callback symptom follows directly from the same stale true value; do not promote the dispatcher in the ranking once the paired-setter polarity evidence is established.

When source-history or diff evidence is available, confirm the injected change against the paired setters: a clean version writing False and using the identical control-flow predicate for both direction is the expected repair shape.
skill.trigger: Investigate when disabling or stopping an object leaves it enabled/started, or when a documented no-op action appears to do the opposite; use this when a single true/false state key is written by two similarly named public methods.

skill.title: Constructor stores transformed input copies in Object attributes
knowledge: Inspect the constructor of the affected data class (e.g. parso/tree.py Leaf.__init__) assignment by assignment: `self.value = value[::-1]`, `self.start_pos = (start_pos[1], start_pos[0])`, `self.prefix = prefix.upper()` are direct symptoms; basic correctness expects `self.value = value`, `self.start_pos = start_pos`, `self.prefix = prefix`.

Grep the module and repository for the same transforms used in the assignments—`[::-1]`, tuple reversal, `.upper()`/`.lower()`. If no other occurrence provides an inverse/compensating operation, the constructor's mutation is not part of a legitimate encode/decode pair.

Trace subclasses and convenience factories (TypedLeaf, ErrorLeaf, parser token factories). If they forward raw `value`, `start_pos`, `prefix` straight to `super().__init__`, the leaf constructor remains the only place the corruption can originate.

Follow the parser conversion path from the token source to the constructed object (`Parser.convert_leaf`/`_add_token` calls like `Leaf(value, start_pos, prefix)`). When token values arrive untouched, a simple parse probe (`x = 1` and printing each leaf) exposes the corruption on first construction, confirming initialization-time contamination rather than an external mutation.

If a package build directory or prior packaged copy exists (e.g. `build/lib/parso/tree.py`), inspect the same constructor lines there; plain assignments in the clean copy confirm that the delivered buggy version injected `[::-1]`, swapped tuple, and `.upper()` transformations.

Construct the simplest object directly and inspect its attributes before reading consumers: after `Leaf('hello', (1,5), 'prefix')`, all three attributes are wrong immediately, establishing that the fault is in the state assignments visible in `__init__`.
skill.trigger: When object initialization corrupts field values that should exactly mirror the constructed parameters (e.g. reversed strings, swapped coordinate tuples, uppercased text metadata) and attribute assignment lines contain visible mutations, inspect each constructor assignment against its parameter and verify whether any later transform legitimately compensates.

skill.title: Enum equality helper returns NotImplemented for primitive comparisons
knowledge: When enum member == primitive is False despite the primitive equaling the member's value, locate the module-level function assigned to __eq__ in the enum metaclass and read its full body. If the function handles identity and same-class comparisons but for all other operand types ends in return NotImplemented, the primitive comparison falls through to identity and the observed failure is fully explained without tracing further.

Inspect the metaclass __new__ to confirm how members get their equality: typically a dict built from class attributes is extended with __eq__=<module_eq_fn> and __hash__=<module_hash_fn> before constructing the base enum type. The metaclass is only the wiring point; if all enum classes share the same broken module-level helper, the helper body is the decision point to rank first.

Search the enum module for every use of the equality helper name, __eq__, and __hash__. If the only occurrences are the helper definitions and the metaclass wiring line, there is no alternate override site, and the defect must be inside the equality helper's branch coverage.

Read the enum comparison tests and classify the asserted operand pairs into rows: same object, same-class named members, members of different enum classes that share names or values, and member versus matching primitive. Run the source equality helper's branch outcomes against each row; the primitive row is the one that fails because it exits through the final NotImplemented branch, proving the missing functionality is a value-aware comparison for non-member operands.

If a repair would make enum members equal to their primitive values, check for hashable-enum tests that place enum members and raw primitives as co-existing keys in one dictionary. When member __hash__ hashes the member's name and primitive hashes differ, value-aware equality does not collapse those keys; such tests confirm the hashing helper and metaclass wiring are constraints on the fix, not defect candidates.

When the equality helper carries a TODO or docstring saying it is not yet implemented, treat that as direct evidence of deliberately missing functionality. The localization conclusion is then the helper's incomplete branch coverage, and any neighboring tests or consumer behavior should be used only to infer the intended semantics, not to redirect blame to the metaclass that simply installs the helper.
skill.trigger: Use when an enum regression report says enum member values no longer compare equal to primitive values (e.g., RGB.RED == 1 is False), and the enum module defines member equality through a module-level function attached by the enum metaclass.

fault_subtype: incomplete enum member equality for non-member operands

skill.title: Exception branch ignores flag that controls return tuple arity
knowledge: After reading the reported function, enumerate every return/raise path and check whether each exit preserves the same arity/type contract; a mismatch between success branches and the exception branch is the strongest signature of this fault.

If success exits pass an evaluate/ callback's result through untouched while the except branch returns a hardcoded scalar, verify whether the callback's result depends on the return_all_scores-style flag; if so, the except branch must apply the same conditional shaping.

Grep for the function name and read every in-repo test that mentions it; a parametrized failure test asserting (0.0, [0.0]*len(trainset)) for the flag true and 0.0 for false is authoritative, and should be checked against each branch of the current code before proposing any fix.

For every call site passing the flag as true, look for tuple unpacking/destructuring; if the consumer is only a line like `default_score, results = function(...)`, the sole reason for the tuple is that destructuring, and a scalar return from the exception path will raise TypeError at runtime.

When the issue text and an in-repo test both specify the expected failure value, do not rely on dynamic reproduction; the test assertions plus the destructuring call site are sufficient to localize the defect to the exception branch and to specify the fix (return the flag-dependent tuple conditionally).

Treat unexpected logger additions or variable renaming in surrounding code as noise; the actual defect is the except branch's unconditional return, not the incidental cleanup lines that may appear in the patch.
skill.trigger: Issue reports wrong return value/type/shape when a helper's error handling triggers, particularly when the helper has an optional flag like return_all_scores and callers expect a tuple when that flag is true.

skill.title: Config-accepted callback accepted but one category-specific applier never invokes it while sibling appliers do
knowledge: Grep the repository for the config callback's assigned name to enumerate every helper, schema generator, or field collector that consumes it; list each consumer and read the complete dispatch branch rather than trusting one representative implementation or issue text.

For each helper accepting the raw user callback, verify two properties in the plain-callable branch: the callback is actually invoked with the item's name (e.g. alias = alias_generator(name)), and target locals such as alias/validation_alias/serialization_alias are seeded to None before the type dispatch. A variant with neither property cannot populate any metadata and may read an unbound local in its later guards.

When one helper lacks call-plus-initialization while a directly adjacent twin on the same source page has both, treat the sibling as the specification: the bug is in the one variant that reads a target local before assigning it and then assigns that local to the live metadata object, not in the later assignment code.

Look for the actual in-place write that propagates generated metadata to the returned/persisted metadata object (e.g. field_info.alias = alias). If that write exists but the branch that should set the local never calls the callback, the missing call is the responsible fault and the visible write only sharpens the anomaly.

Rule out config preprocessing as an alternative explanation: check the config option's declared type allows the raw callback, and search for constructions that could wrap it into a richer generator object. If no wrapper is ever constructed, the raw callback takes the suspected applier branch directly.

Find the call sites that invoke the applier helpers: if all model/dataclass/TypedDict field schemas funnel through one shared mutation site that calls the broken helper with the live metadata object, then no later override can explain the uniformly unset aliases and the fault is localized to that helper.

Search tests that exercise the callback: assertions on alias-key validation or by_alias serialization prove the callback must be invoked, and an exact exception string from a presence check (e.g. 'must return str') identifies which guard the implementation expects to reach *after* the callback returns. Use that contract to distinguish a variant whose guard is present but whose call line is missing.

When the issue report says the callback 'is being called' but source shows no call, do not assume the report's runtime symptom; verify whether the uninitialized local would raise when schema generation runs and compare that with tests to decide whether the observable failure is an exception or silently missing aliases.

Use source-reading as the decisive comparison once greps, tests, and call-site tracing consistently point to the helper family; the strongest evidence is reading the complete callable branch in the failing helper side-by-side with its correctly implemented sibling.
skill.trigger: Use when config exposes a user-supplied transformation callback (e.g. alias_generator) that is supposed to shape metadata for fields, but generated values are unset or the path raises an unexpected UnboundLocalError/NameError. Use when search shows multiple near-identical helper methods consume the same callback for different item kinds (fields, computed fields, function arguments) and only some actually call it. Also use when tests assert the callback runs or when metadata is read from the model after a helper was supposed to mutate it.

fault_subtype: config callback omitted from one category-specific applier variant

skill.title: Local variable read before assignment due to unconditional early return preceding all bindings
knowledge: Grep for the exact variable name from the error message, then within each function sort the hit lines by line number; any assignment inside a Python function makes that name function-local, so an earlier read with no executed assignment is a candidate for exactly this UnboundLocalError.

Read the complete enclosing function body rather than stopping at the grep hit; if an unconditional return precedes every assignment, the failure is structural and fires on every call, so reproducing it does not require any special input.

Do not let a malformed or scrambled dead-code tail distract localization: when an unconditional return precedes the assignments, every later statement is unreachable, and each variable the tail was meant to bind is unbound at the return.

List callers of the broken function and expect them to merely unpack, iterate, or propagate the exception; rank the callee that creates and returns the value above loader callers that forward control flow into it.

Use neighboring code that consumes the same token layout as an independent contract check: if another function passes a parsed value range and an is-extended flag into the message constructor, that confirms the broken function's intended two-value return and which statements in its dead tail are relevant to repair.

Trace callers up to the public loader entry point to explain why all operations fail; if every loading, converting, and code-generation path routes through the broken parser function for each ID-bearing message, the observed worldwide failure is fully explained by one callee.
Search for duplicate definitions of the enclosing function across format modules to ensure grep hits point to the single active implementation before ranking a candidate.

Alternative hypothesis to consider only when a write exists earlier in source: if that write is under a conditional, exception path, or nonlocal scope, trace reachable control flow from function entry to the first read before blaming the later write; line-order evidence alone is sufficient only when no reachable write precedes the read.
skill.trigger: When a Python traceback reports UnboundLocalError for a local variable, and a literal grep for that variable name shows a return statement that reads it before any assignment in the same function, with assignments located later in the function body.

skill.title: UnboundLocalError/NameError from statement-order-corrupted leaf functions
knowledge: For each failing local name, read the whole containing function's source in order and list every reference to that name; if a reference appears before any assignment/binding of that same name in that scope, the body has scrambled or removed statements and every call through the failing branch will crash.

Treat early unconditional returns as suspicious when their returned object is not assigned earlier in the same body; if the return appears textually before the assignment and before real function documentation/body, the early 'success' fragment is misplaced code rather than a valid fast path.

When multiple independent local names are used but never assigned in the same function (e.g., a message built for an exception, a codec/table entry pair, or a temporary tag buffer), classify the function itself as corrupted before investigating its callers; such calls appear healthy precisely because they pass control to a leaf whose body is scrambled.

Search for intended definitions that are absent from the body, not just for late assignments: confirm by looking for roles like 'build an error message from parameters', 'look up writer callback+parameter from a dispatch map', or 'assign the special tag bytes before a startswith check'. Their use sites remain visible while their assignment lines were deleted, producing the reported NameError/UnboundLocalError.

Check exactly one reported exception at a time against the same source range and confirm no earlier assignment was hidden in a preceding branch, argument default, or module-level import/global; if absent, the leaf function is the responsible fix site and caller-side wrappers need not be rewritten.

After naming the corrupted function, inspect whether it is called by several untouched functions further down the file; if those callers look structurally intact and simply delegate to the corrupted leaf, stop scanning there and place the repair in the leaf's statement order.
skill.trigger: Use when reported errors are UnboundLocalError or NameError for a local name at runtime, and the highest-value next clue is checking that same function's body in source order.

skill.title: Dot-prefixed directories omitted from local index search because enumeration loop skips them before pattern matching
knowledge: Follow the public search entry point until it reaches the layout object's get_recipes_references role (directory enumeration/reference builder). In conans/client/rest_client_local_recipe_index.py this is _LocalRecipesIndexLayout.get_recipes_references, the only routine that lists the `<base>/recipes` directory, filters entries, and constructs RecipeReference objects that feed the search response.

In that routine inspect the lines between the os.listdir-style directory listing and the subsequent fnmatch-style pattern check. Search for `startswith(".")`, often written as `if r.startswith("."): continue`. A guard placed there prevents hidden recipe folders from ever reaching the pattern match, so that loop is the defect boundary.

Do not treat os.listdir itself as the hiding mechanism: os.listdir returns dot-prefixed entries unless something explicitly filters them. The observed omission must come from a separate dot-name skip guard or from an upstream caller/root-layout pre-filtering that supplies a reduced directory list.

Use presence or absence of the dot-name guard as branch evidence. In some snapshots the reported dot-name guard may not be present in the code that was actually read; when that happens, verify the concrete behavior by checking whether a hidden recipe path under `recipes/.hidden_recipe/config.yml` with pattern `*` produces a reference. If it does not, inspect upstream callers or the local clone/layout source before modifying the loop, because the responsibility may lie elsewhere.

When the guard is found, confirm that its removal is intended by checking adjacent comments and tests in local-recipes-index functional/integration tests. The expected behavior is that any valid recipe directory (contains config.yml / version info) participates in matching regardless of a leading dot; skipping should be reserved for structurally invalid entries, not hidden names.

Distinguish a filtered enumeration from a path-shaped problem: this skill applies when the missing entries are ordinary recipe folders whose names start with a dot. If a consumer or searcher transforms a dot-prefixed pattern or path in a way that mismatches the physical path, then the localization should move to path construction/normalization rather than the directory-listing loop.
skill.trigger: When a local index/search API is reported to omit dot-prefixed recipe directories (or files) from results, and the search results are built by enumerating a base recipes directory and filtering each entry by a name pattern.

skill.title: Exception constructors and __str__ methods encode message state that contradicts reachable raising paths and formatting flags
knowledge: When a report concerns multiple exception messages within one library, open the exception module's constructors and __str__ methods first; several defects may share one file, as with the not-found exception's default message and the syntax-error exception's formatting method.

For a not-found message such as 'some templates given were found', grep the exact phrase across the repository. If it appears only inside the default-message branch of the exception constructor, inspect the construction sites and their control flow: a loader loop that raises only after every candidate name fails contradicts the word 'some' and places the fault in that constructor branch rather than in the caller.

In the not-found exception constructor, also compare the assigned exception state to test expectations: a buggy `parent.__init__(names[0])` plus `self.templates = list(reversed(names))` violates tests that assert the caller-order `.templates` list and the last attempted name. Use those assertions as evidence of intended state assignment, not as repair instructions.

For syntax-error text formatting, read the exception's `__str__` before searching for alternate formatters. Verify which path actually runs by grepping assignments to the exception's `translated` flag: a traceback-rewriting helper that sets `translated = True` and attaches `source` is what activates the formatted branch for syntax errors raised during compilation.

Grep for the source-line lookup by its characteristic call, e.g., `splitlines()`. If the only occurrence is inside the target exception `__str__`, no competing formatter can be responsible, and the method must contain the observable message faults.

When a strategy list of formatting fixes is reported (wrong join separator, off-by-one line number, inverted filename condition, unstripped source, inverted translated condition), inspect every corresponding expression in the disputed method; all five being present in one method is strong evidence the method alone is the fault surface.

Search the test suite for assertions that pattern-match exception messages or state (e.g., `.templates`, `e.value.name`, or specific substrings). These tests provide a public contract for how the exception must be constructed, distinguishing a state-assignment bug from a loader or caller bug.
skill.trigger: A bug report describes multiple inconsistent exception messages in one library, e.g., a not-found exception saying 'some items were found' when the code path implies none were found, plus a syntax-error __str__ with wrong separators, off-by-one line numbers, inverted guards, and unstripped source. Use this skill when initial exception classes are plausible and before chasing callers or custom formatters.

skill.title: State handler appends token then returns EOF sentinel
knowledge: When clean/linkify input containing entities returns empty or mangled output, treat the tokenizer's token-production boundary as the first suspect; determine whether the affected input ever reaches filters or serializers by tracing the driver loop before ranking later-stage token consumers.

Characterize a tokenizer driver loop by its iteration condition and where the token queue is drained: if a state handler returning a stop/False sentinel exits before the queue is drained, that handler itself can drop a just-appended token plus all remaining input.

For the special character that triggers the bug, read all sibling states handling that same character across data, rcdata, rawtext, and script modes; a continue/True return after consuming an entity in one mode and a stop/False return in another is a strong signal, and the handler that appends then returns stop is the localization target.

A state handler that appends to the output queue, or calls a helper that appends, must return continue; any such handler returning the EOF/stop sentinel is anomalous even if it also performs a valid-looking state transition.

When a source comment states that the loop terminates when a state returns False, connect that comment to the symptom literally: input beginning with the triggering character disappears before any token is drained, so do not require an additional downstream filter to explain the empty output.

If an intentional override re-emits a character back into the stream, verify where that re-emitted character is consumed before ranking the override; an intentional no-op explains what token is produced but not why tokenization stops, so inspect the state invoked after the override returns.

Trace a tiny concrete reference through state transitions: current state routing on the triggering character, the next state's append action, and that state's return value; mark whether queue append occurs and whether the loop can drain before the next iteration to identify the exact point where a pending token is lost.

Before choosing a repair, compare with the canonical twin handler: canonical entity consumption switches state and returns continue; if the suspect vendored handler returns stop, changing its tail to match the twin and restoring the continue return is the minimal repair, then verify downstream consumers receive the entity token.
skill.trigger: HTML cleaning or linkification returns empty output specifically when input contains entities/character references, and the project uses a tokenizer whose generator loop runs while a state function returns a continue sentinel and drains its output queue only inside that loop.

skill.title: Subclass declared without its required base class while the base import remains dangling
knowledge: Read the target class's module end-to-end and list every self.<name> referenced in its methods. If none of those names is defined in the module or installed in a local __init__, the class must obtain them through inheritance; an empty-parens declaration such as 'class SomeGrant():' is therefore a structural defect candidate.

Search for the module's imports and then grep within the module for each imported base-like name excluding its import line. A base-class symbol that occurs only in the import statement is a dangling import, strongly suggesting the base was removed from the class declaration rather than never needed.

Run a declaration-line grep over the package/directory containing sibling classes (e.g., regex '^class \w+Grant.*\(') and compare bases. If all siblings inherit the same common base while the target class appears alone with empty parens or no base, the target's declaration is the anomaly and should be ranked first.

Locate the common base class and inspect its __init__ and helper methods. If the base assigns exactly the attributes the target's body references (e.g., request_validator, token modifiers, custom validators) and defines the helper methods the target calls (e.g., default headers, grant/scope validation), the base is the missing dependency and the fix is confined to the one declaration line.

Rank the missing-base declaration itself as the primary defect; rank the target's methods that read those missing attributes as symptoms, not separate defects, because rewriting method bodies cannot supply the state the base constructor installs.

Consider the alternative that the defect is method-local only when the class already inherits the suspected base or when the referenced state/helpers are defined elsewhere in the module. The combination of empty-parens declaration, dangling base import, and sibling inheritance distinguishes missing-base from behavioral/logic bugs.

When siblings override a method that the target also defines, compare the target's method body to a sibling's only if the inheritance link is already confirmed; otherwise the inheritance defect explains method failures and further body diffing does not change fault localization.
skill.trigger: When a class body uses self.* attributes or methods that are not defined anywhere in that module and the class has no __init__, and a base-class-like name is imported but appears otherwise unused, especially when sibling classes in the same package are declared with a common base.

knowledge: Inspect the constructor of the affected data class assignment by assignment: each attribute assignment should place its constructor argument into the attribute verbatim. Flag any assignment whose right-hand side transforms the argument (e.g., `self.value = value[::-1]`, `self.start_pos = (start_pos[1], start_pos[0])`, `self.prefix = prefix.upper()`). Trace the boundary between the token stream and the constructed object: locate every place that instantiates the leaf class (e.g., `convert_leaf`/`default_leaf` in parser code) and verify that raw token arguments (value, start_pos, prefix) are passed through unchanged. If all construction sites forward raw arguments, the corruption must occur in the constructor itself or in the tokenizer; the constructor's store logic distinguishes the two.

skill.title: Emitter output contradicts its paired in-file parser contract
knowledge: When a serialization layer has multiple per-consumer formatters and the corresponding parser for each consumer is embedded in the same source file, treat the embedded parser as the wire contract. For each candidate formatter, read its paired parser first, note the exact field order and separators the parser splits on, then hand-feed representative items with and without help through the formatter and parse the resulting string with that parser. A formatter that disagrees only with its own parser is thereby identified directly from source reading.

If a direct grep for the suspected formatter method name in tests returns nothing, search using the vocabulary of the bug symptom instead of the internal method name and read the parametrized end-to-end test. Its exact expected output strings, including both item-with-help and item-without-help cases, are the wire contract at emitted-text granularity. Compute what each formatter would emit for those same items and compare: each mismatch ranks a formatter, while the matching siblings are confirmed uninvolved in one read.

A generic base pipeline that only joins or dispatches formatter output, with no shared field construction, is evidence that the corruptions are local expressions inside each per-consumer formatter. When every variant is wrong only against its own paired parser and the common path is intact, rank the per-variant formatter methods rather than searching for one shared root cause.

After isolating the failing formatters, continue auditing the rest of that file's producer/parser boundary, especially the earlier stage that decides which items are passed to the formatters. Read predicates for contradictory negations, duplicated calls whose loop scopes are disjoint, or reversed iteration. Such discrepancies localize corruption in a selection-stage function even if the visible test matrix does not exercise that path, making it a co-responsible candidate to rank or mention beside the formatters.
skill.trigger: Use when multiple per-consumer serializers in one source file feed consumer-specific parsers embedded in the same file (for example shell source templates), and symptoms are consumer-specific: wrong field order, wrong separator, or a help/placeholder branch that produces no usable completion. Also useful more broadly when candidate code contains a producer/consumer wire format and tests may pin the exact serialized text.

skill.title: Exception branch ignores flag that controls return tuple arity
knowledge: After reading the reported function, enumerate every return/raise path and check whether each exit preserves the same arity/type contract; a mismatch between success branches and the exception branch is the strongest signature of this fault.

If success exits pass an evaluate/ callback's result through untouched while the except branch returns a hardcoded scalar, verify whether the callback's result depends on the return_all_scores-style flag; if so, the except branch must apply the same conditional shaping.

Grep for the function name and read every in-repo test that mentions it; a parametrized failure test asserting (0.0, [0.0]*len(trainset)) for the flag true and 0.0 for false is authoritative, and should be checked against each branch of the current code before proposing any fix.

For every call site passing the flag as true, look for tuple unpacking/destructuring; if the consumer is only a line like `default_score, results = function(...)`, the sole reason for the tuple is that destructuring, and a scalar return from the exception path will raise TypeError at runtime.

When the issue text and an in-repo test both specify the expected failure value, do not rely on dynamic reproduction; the test assertions plus the destructuring call site are sufficient to localize the defect to the exception branch and to specify the fix (return the flag-dependent tuple conditionally).

Treat unexpected logger additions or variable renaming in surrounding code as noise; the actual defect is the except branch's unconditional return, not the incidental cleanup lines that may appear in the patch.
skill.trigger: Issue reports wrong return value/type/shape when a helper's error handling triggers, particularly when the helper has an optional flag like return_all_scores and callers expect a tuple when that flag is true.

skill.title: Exception branch ignores flag that controls return tuple arity

When scanning the module, do not let sibling helpers that do not delegate to the target (e.g., a `..._with_pruning` wrapper) or incidental noise in surrounding code confuse the localization; the defect is the unexpected scalar return in the exception branch.

skill.title: Return references a local never assigned in the function body
knowledge: When a function's body contains only a raise branch followed by `return local_name`, grep the same variable and verify whether any assignment appears in that function's scope. If all assignments live in callers or sibling plot classes, the return is structurally unbound and the producer is incomplete: every call that skips the raise exits with UnboundLocalError, which is visible from a single source read without execution.

Trace the default/no-argument route through the shared setup to distinguish normal defaults from invalid input: find where the relevant argument is popped with a sentinel default, confirm the validation helper maps that sentinel to None (meaning 'not provided by the user'), and watch that None flow into the suspicious producer. If this route is shared by other plot kinds that still work, the shared plumbing is exonerated and the candidate-specific producer must be the fault site.

Expect the repair to add assignment branches between the conflict check and the return, including a no-color/default branch that maps an rcParam facecolor default into the return value. Do not expect the downstream plotting call to supply the default, because the function must return a concrete value before the plotting call consumes it.
skill.trigger: A likely producer function ends with `return local_name` while the only preceding code is a validation or conflict check that raises in one branch. All other argument paths exit through that return, so calls with valid/default arguments fail with UnboundLocalError rather than a downstream validation error.

skill.title: Directory file discovery skips valid files due to path-form mismatch in extension or ignore filtering
knowledge: Reproduce the discovery through its public directory entry point on a controlled directory containing only one matching-extension file, and observe whether the result is empty, incomplete, or includes wrong files.
Trace the public discovery entry into its low-level helpers for traversal, exact-path handling, extension matching, and ignore-spec loading rather than assuming the bug is in traversal logic.

Use the first observable divergence from expected behavior to identify which filtering layer rejects the file, then compare the path representation entering that layer to the documented or intended one.
Inspect extension predicates for subtle path-form assumptions: a leading ./ prefix, absolute-versus-relative mismatch, or OS-specific separator can make every valid extension test fail.

If ignore patterns seem to suppress valid files, verify whether the ignore matcher receives absolute, relative, or normalized paths and confirm that all call sites use the same path form as the ignore-spec loader.

Directly invoke the suspected helper predicates with controlled inputs to determine which one returns false and what path form it actually expects; this avoids debugging the whole discovery pipeline at once.
skill.trigger: Use when directory traversal or file discovery returns an empty or unexpected file set, or when extension matching / ignore-file processing stops finding expected files after refactoring.

skill.title: Filter excludes all valid items because it checks a key or attribute that valid inputs never carry
knowledge: Reproduce the routine through its public entry point on a minimal input that should produce output, and observe whether the result is empty, incomplete, or contains wrong items; an empty result from a valid input is the first sign of an over-restrictive filter.

Trace the public entry into the filtering loop or helper that decides which items are included, and inspect the guard condition against the actual structure of the input items; a guard that checks a key or attribute that valid items never carry will skip every item.

Use the routine's own docstring or examples as an executable specification: walk the documented input through the guard by hand and count the produced items; if the count contradicts the documented output, the guard is the fault location.

Compare the suspected filter against a reference implementation or equivalent helper that performs the same transformation without the extra guard; if the reference includes all items and the filter excludes them, the guard is responsible.

Inspect the test fixtures or representative inputs to confirm which keys or attributes they actually carry; if the guard's required key is absent from all valid inputs, the guard is unconditionally false and the filter is broken.

When the filter checks a key that is only sometimes present, verify whether the absence should mean 'include' or 'exclude' by consulting the documented contract and the reference implementation, not by assuming the guard's intent.
skill.trigger: Use when an expansion, discovery, or conversion routine returns an empty or unexpectedly incomplete result because a filter condition tests a key, attribute, or path form that the valid inputs do not actually possess (e.g., missing metadata key, wrong path representation, or absent attribute).

skill.title: Entity constructor reads __slots__ attribute before assigning it
knowledge: When a reported failing set consists of thin wrapper methods whose terminal data-construction argument is the same entity type (e.g., data_type=Tweet), compare them with adjacent unreported wrappers that pass a different entity type (e.g., data_type=User). If the failing set matches one entity type exactly, stop inspecting the wrapper internals or request helpers and rank that entity's constructor as the fault point.

For a model class using __slots__ with a mapping-style __getattr__ fallback, inspect __init__ for slot-assignment order: each slot should be assigned from the payload (self.<slot> = data.get(...)) before any `if self.<slot> is not None:` conversion guard appears. A guard reading an unassigned slot is a defect because normal attribute lookup finds an empty slot, __getattr__ delegates to the backing data mapping, and a missing payload key then raises AttributeError from inside the constructor.

Confirm the intended healthy pattern in a sibling entity constructor whose methods do not fail: it assigns every slot exactly once immediately before its guards. The dangling guards without preceding assignments are the responsible source; the presence of working API wrappers that construct this model means the issue is not an unbound endpoint or missing mapping, even when the reported symptom is AttributeError on method invocation.
skill.trigger: API/client methods that should return entities of one model all raise AttributeError while sibling methods returning another entity type succeed, and the error names what looks like an entity data attribute rather than a missing client method.

skill.title: Empty classification suppresses taxonomy page-index generation before root-dirname exception can apply
knowledge: Inspect the taxonomy decision method that determines whether a classification page should be generated (the should_generate_classification_page role) before editing other code. Look for an early empty-post-list guard conditional on omit_empty_classifications placed before a later root or empty-dirname exception (for example, if dirname == '': return True). With that ordering, an empty root classification hits the first return False and the later exception is unreachable, making the local method an independently sufficient defect.

Grep for the callers of that decision method and read the task-generation loop. Callers may precompute generation flags with their own `if len(filtered_posts) == 0 and taxonomy.omit_empty_classifications:` branch and disable the list/rss/atom tasks before ever invoking the per-taxonomy decision method. If that short-circuit exists, fixing only the method's guard ordering leaves empty classifications, including root entries, suppressed.

Trace whether control actually reaches the decision method for an empty root classification: if it is not reached, the caller-side precompute is responsible for the suppression; if it is reached with an empty post list, the method's internal ordering is responsible. Both conditions can coexist, so after reading the actual source rank both causes instead of assuming one patch cures the observed missing page. Confirm whether empty-dirname means the root page and whether the relevant plugin enables omit_empty_classifications by default.
skill.trigger: When a taxonomy, directory, or page-index page is missing for an empty classification or for a root/empty-dirname entry, especially with omit_empty_classifications enabled and a decision method that appears to have a rule for still generating the root page.

skill.title: Consumer references a generator variable whose producer block is absent from the function
knowledge: Read the full function from the parameter list to the consumption seam after finding a NameError/UnboundLocalError for a consumed variable. The defect is visible when the variable appears in a comprehension or loop but is never assigned in the function body, while signature options meant to feed it (pixel-array source, codec/plugin names, keyword options) have no later use. A consumer line immediately following an '# Encode!' or similar comment is a strong indicator that the producer block was deleted between the validation preamble and the consumption line.

Distinguish a deleted producer from a moved or helper-supplied one by grepping the whole repository for the consumed variable and for the generator-producing API the local documentation or test path mentions. If the variable's source occurrences are only the consumer plus documentation/test copies, and the intended producer API has no callers outside its own definition, the function containing the consumer is the responsible implementation. If any producer assignment or caller exists elsewhere, trace that reachable call path before blaming the consumer.

Reconstruct the missing block's required behavior from documentation tracebacks and from guard strings that appear only in tests. When a documentation traceback routes from the public wrapper through this same function into the generator-producing API, and exact messages for pre-checks appear only under test files rather than under source files, those tests specify a contract that only the deleted block implements—such as raising when required transfer/metadata fields are absent on a source-route, or bypassing those checks when an in-memory array is supplied. Comparing those contracts with the existing helper for constructing options reveals whether the deleted route prepared a source object or an array before calling the producer.
skill.trigger: A function performs its main encoding/transform by iterating over a local variable (for example `encoded = [f for f in frame_iterator]`) after an options/validation preamble, but no statement in the function ever binds that variable and no other producer appears in the repository. Calls raise NameError, and source reading reveals an empty seam between the preamble and the consumer.

skill.title: Command run() reads local variables before moved argument assignment
knowledge: For each command entry-point run() method, trace every local used on its success and error paths and locate where each is assigned in source order. If a name such as module, filename, or spidercls is read after only the arg-count check and has no binding before that read anywhere in the method, the run() body raises NameError and should be ranked highest over intact-looking helpers.

Treat the command tests' expected outputs as the required sequencing contract: file creation after successful arg parsing; messages like "File not found:", "No spider found in file:", and "Unable to load"; reactor and event-loop lines emitted after crawler startup. If the tests expect those outcomes but the run() body either uses an unbound local or calls crawl/start before validation, the defect is the run() body's assignment/validation order, not the missing file, crawler helper, or reactor-selection code.

Before blaming a definition-only helper, grep for its call sites and inspect the arguments at those calls. A helper that is never invoked, or is invoked with an unbound variable, is exonerated; the call belongs inside Command.run(). Similarly, if reactor/asyncio log lines are emitted downstream of crawler_process.start(), a command that dies before reaching start cannot be fixed by changing reactor-installation helpers.
skill.trigger: Applicable when a CLI/command regression affects multiple user-visible behaviors (spider generation, file-not-found messaging, reactor/event-loop logging), command helper methods look intact, and the suspicious Command.run() body contains local-name reads whose assignments may have been moved below the reads.

skill.title: Validation guard references a context flag that was never assigned
knowledge: When a fault report names an identifier in a NameError, grep the whole repository for that exact literal identifier. If the only matches are right-hand-side uses inside expressions and there is no `identifier = ...`, parameter, import, function/class name, or global, the name is an unbound local of the enclosing function. Read the full body of that function; the missing assignment is inside it, not in its callers or wrappers.

For a guard such as `if operand_1 and dangling_name:` or `if dangling_name and operand_1:`, identify what the other operand depends on. When it is an isinstance/value-kind check, the guard is type-sensitive: the dangling name is evaluated only for values that fail the earlier check, and scalar or primitive paths short-circuit before reaching it. Use that to explain why the reproducer only crashes for lists, dicts, or other structured values.

Trace the context argument (for example, a key or discriminator) that the validator uses to allow or reject whole-structure interpolation. Whole-structure resolvers call the interpolation/validation path with a default or missing context value while ordinary scalar entries pass a concrete key. If the validator's own policy depends on that context value, contains the explanatory error text, and is the only place enforcing the rule, rank the validator above the wrappers and callers that merely forward or catch its errors.
skill.trigger: A NameError names a variable that appears in a validation condition. The failure is type- or path-sensitive, and the surrounding function reads like it should know the context through a boolean flag or discriminator that is never set.

fault_subtype: missing context-flag assignment leaves an unbound local in a validation guard

skill.title: Row serializer returns an expression with an invalid string operator
knowledge: Read the function that serializes each entity to a row: grep for the symbol named at the call site or for the row terminator, then use source reading to inspect its final return expression rather than only its field construction. If the return is `",".join(fields) - "\n"`, both operands are strings and every invocation is an unconditional TypeError, independent of entity state.

Distinguish an invalid-operator TypeError from a join-content TypeError by checking how the joined elements are constructed. If every element is a string literal or returned by a string-formatting call, the terminal operator is the only raising site; a join failure would instead identify the offending sequence index ('sequence item N: expected str instance').

Map the backend aggregation path to see why the crash appears only after entities are created: the backend function that concatenates header plus rows may loop only over existing entities, so tests with no entities avoid the serializer entirely. Confirming the row serializer has a single call site and that the reproduced path creates an entity first fixes the ranked candidate set.

Verify the intended wire format from consumers or tests before fixing: if existing tests parse `header == report.split("\n")[0]` and feed `csv.DictReader` on newline-separated lines, rows must be newline-delimited. The correct repair is in the row serializer's terminator, not in upstream field-value producers or in field formatting.
skill.trigger: When a report or generated text is assembled by looping over created entities and raises TypeError at the retrieve/get stage, inspect the row serializer's final return expression for an invalid arithmetic operator between string operands before investigating data values or formatting.

skill.title: Inverted boolean return in a stateful comparison method
knowledge: Inspect the method's own docstring/comment and independently trace its reachable return paths for the first call, an equal-value call, and a changed-value call. If the implementation returns True exactly when the previous state equals the incoming value but the documented contract promises True when they differ, the condition or branch order is inverted, and the fault is localized to that method rather than to caller loop bookkeeping.

Verify how the stored previous-value state is initialized. If it uses a unique sentinel (e.g., a module-level `missing` object), confirm that `sentinel == user_value` is never true; then the equality branch can fire only on repeated values. That makes the first-call and changed-call traces conclusive from the source page alone.

Search for all definitions and assignments of the state attribute (e.g., grep for `def changed` and `_last_changed_value`) to confirm there is a single method and no other writer of that state. If an async or alternative loop context inherits the method without overriding it, one fix at the single definition resolves behavior in both sync and async paths.

Look for unit tests that enumerate the expected True/False output for a known input sequence; use them as an independent contract to distinguish a method-body inversion from iteration-state or caller misuse. A test that reports the exact per-item booleans is the strongest non-source confirmation.
skill.trigger: When a method that compares a new value against previously stored state returns True for unchanged/equal values and False for a change or first call, check the method body's condition branches against its own contract and trace the first, equal, and changed cases.

skill.title: Expected output columns are absent because removed feature logic left an orphaned section comment and a dead local assignment
knowledge: Open the method that builds the product's output columns/fields and inspect the region under section comments. If a descriptive comment such as '# check for feature' is immediately followed by an assignment to a local that is never read later (for example a boolean initialized to False), treat it as residue of removed parsing logic. Grep the repository for that local's name; a single occurrence in source proves the block is dead rather than evidence of live behavior.

Grep for the expected output column names to determine whether any production code still extracts those input fields. If the names appear only in test assertions and documentation, no parser anywhere reads them, so the repair must restore their extraction and inclusion at the method that is actually reachable for the reported input type.

Verify the file-type dispatch to identify the sole output-building parser for the reported input (for example HDF5/NetCDF to one method, FITS to another). Compare the observed partially populated column list with the column/units structures each builder constructs; the builder whose output exactly matches the observed columns and is reachable from the reported file is the top-ranked location. An intact sibling builder for the other file type is evidence of the pre-regression implementation shape but should not be patched.

Use in-repo contract tests as the executable specification: a test that loads the reported fixture and asserts the missing column pins down the expected output, and companion tests that assert every output column has an associated unit force any repair to add both the data column and its corresponding units-table entry. Changelog entries associating the feature class or parser with the behavior confirm this is a regression of previously supported functionality rather than a new feature request.
skill.trigger: Use when parsed or constructed output is missing feature columns/fields that tests or docs say should be present, and the method that builds the output structure still contains a stale descriptive comment immediately followed by a local variable that is assigned but never read again. Also use when a file-type dispatch sends the reported input to exactly one builder and grepping for the expected column names returns only tests/documentation, never production code.

fault_subtype: dead stub and missing expected output columns in the sole output-building parser

skill.title: Authentication failure is raised when the preceding authentication helper just succeeded
knowledge: Find every raise site of the authentication exception first; if exactly one exists, read the code just before it: a call like `self.key = self.authenticate(self.password)` followed by `if self.key is not None: raise AuthenticationFailed` is an inverted guard, but do not judge it until you read the helper's return contract. Successful authentication returns key bytes; failed authentication returns None. That return contract makes the inversion unambiguous and shifts suspicion from crypto/password logic to the guard itself.

Check whether subclasses/implementations for each format or security version override the initializer that contains the guarded raise. If they all inherit the base method and the registry routes every version through it, the single inverted branch explains the full symptom range (RC4, AES-128, AES-256, user and owner passwords) and should be ranked as the sole localization.

Use the helper's clean key-bytes-or-None return value as a discriminator: if the helper internally encapsulates hashing/AES/derivation and returns None only for failed verification, there is no need to audit the crypto itself. Strong evidence against an alternative password-preprocessing defect is that every authentication path already produces the expected None-vs-key result, so only the guard's polarity remains wrong.

To confirm the exception surfaces where the user observes it, trace the object construction path: a document-level `Encrypt` entry causes a factory to instantiate the handler, and the handler's constructor calls `init`, which invokes this initializer and raises. This path check is supplementary; the inverted condition plus inherited scope already identifies the responsible line.
skill.trigger: Apply when an authentication/password/credential exception appears to be raised for valid inputs (e.g., wrong passwords are accepted, valid passwords rejected), and the check sits immediately after a helper call in a base-class initializer that may be shared by multiple variants.

skill.title: Mapping diff/merge helper evaluates branches against the wrong side or wrong control flow
knowledge: In a diff-like helper iterating over one mapping, examine each per-key branch’s control flow in the source body. If an ignored/excluded key is handled with `break`, the loop stops after the first ignored key and every later key is silently omitted; `continue` is what actually skips only that key. Use this distinction to rank a loop-control defect inside the helper over caller problems.

Establish which side the helper must report by reading the caller’s comments/docstrings and the expected-output tests before judging assignments. In the differing-scalar branch, check whether the stored value is read from the base/left mapping (`left[k]`) or from the comparison/right mapping (`right.get(k, left[k])`); a right-side read contradicts a documented left-side diff contract and fails tests whose expected output contains only left values.

For recursive pairwise comparisons, trace whether the result of recursion is assigned back into the parent difference. If the recursive result is computed but only referenced in a dead guard—for example `if recursive_result is None: store left[k]` when the helper can never return `None`—then every real nested difference is dropped. A distinguishing read is finding the recursive variable never used in any subsequent assignment.
skill.trigger: When a helper compares two mappings/configs/objects and returns unexpected differences, especially when an ignore/exclude parameter is used, when expected values come from one input but output contains the other, or when nested differences are missing entirely.

skill.title: File-like base class reports capability or position from a fabricated constant rather than from implementation or state
knowledge: When a reusable file/stream base class reports a capability, compare it with the same class's corresponding operation before assigning the bug: if seekable() returns True but seek() unconditionally raises 'File does not support seeking', the unconditional capability constant is the suspect; expected default is False unless a real seek is overridden.

Map the subclass surface with grep for 'def seekable|def seek|def tell' and 'class .*\(BufferedFile\)' (or equivalent). Only subclasses that override both the capability and a real implementation of the capability should report it; a non-overriding subclass provides the expected base default by inheritance. Attribute the defect to the base method when all non-overriding subclasses require the opposite of the current return.

For a position or size getter showing an unexplained offset, inventory every state assignment (grep the position field name or scan increment sites) before ranking the getter. If all updates assign exact byte counts or known absolute positions and none adds the offset, a tell()-style '+1' is fabricated by the getter itself; verify a fresh instance renders 0 and repo-wide grep shows no subclass override of tell that could compensate.

A committed failing test may not exist for the getter; rely on internal consistency contracts instead: a subclass that overrides real seek resets the position to 0 after seek(0), append mode assigns the position to size, and corrected capability defaults align with non-overriding concrete subclasses in checked-in tests.
skill.trigger: A reusable file/stream base class exposes a boolean capability or numeric position getter whose return appears hard-coded: one method contradicts the same class's actual behavior or every recorded state transition.

knowledge: Source-grep for the unsupported type and for the module's accepted-content union name, rather than searching only by the error text. In this pattern a single grep exposed an accepted-content type alias, a sibling streaming path already guarding that type, and dedicated tests for both paths. Existing aware sites are contract evidence that support was intended; the missing functionality is localized to the one conversion path whose isinstance guard omits that type.

Read the conversion choke point used by the constructor before the body is sent, e.g. `self.body = self.render(content)`. Inspect its exact branches: None produces empty bytes, one base byte-type is returned directly, and every other value reaches a catch-all `.encode(charset)` call. An omitted union member is neither of the special-cased branches, so it raises on the encoder it does not have at construction or at the earliest use. This places the fault in the missing branch of that single conversion method and suggests adding the omitted type to its guard.

Rule out downstream sites before ranking: body consumers that only compute `len(body)` or transmit `self.body` without re-encoding cannot reject the omitted type. Check sibling code that already accepts the full union and has a passing test, and confirm which subclasses inherit or override the base conversion. If the only failing construction goes through the base conversion while all other paths accept the type, no alternative fault site is needed.

Treat the type annotation quoted in the issue as a prompt rather than proof. Verify the actual source snapshot, because issue text may describe the pre-defect or intended annotation while the code under investigation has the narrower one; definitive contract evidence comes from the type alias, sibling guards, and dedicated tests.

skill.title: Nested local helper called before its def in the same function
knowledge: In the failing function, list every occurrence of the suspected helper name and compare the line number of its first invocation with the line number of its nested def; because any later local binding makes the name function-local throughout the function, a call textually above the def raises UnboundLocalError at that first call, not NameError.

Confirm the later nested def is not a missing dependency by checking that its signature and return shape match the early calls; when they match, the fault is source reordering of an existing helper, and the fix or ground-truth patch should move all def-side binding above the first call.

Look for a sibling inline function in the same module that uses the same helper-before-all-calls order; the working sibling supplies the intended contract and lets you keep localization inside the out-of-order function instead of following the production class or downstream consumers.

If no top-level definition and no external caller of the failing inline test/callback exists, the runtime failure is guaranteed on direct invocation and investigation can stop at the internal call/def ordering rather than expanding to the feature being tested.
skill.trigger: When a function, especially an inline test/callback function, raises UnboundLocalError for a short helper name invoked several times in its body and a nested def for that name may be present later in the same function.

skill.title: Unbound local from deleted derivation block
knowledge: When a NameError names a local inside the function under inspection, read the whole function from entry to that first read, listing every write to that name, then grep the file for the assignment pattern. If the only writers are in sibling methods and a blank line or code-removal gap sits immediately before the read, the fault is a missing initialization block on all paths, not a package-specific branch or wrong caller.

Read the call site to confirm the printed value is not supplied by the caller; then read the parametrized expected-output tests around the feature. No-package and package-given cases that expect, respectively, the whole object and a dotted subtree/scalar reveal the required derivation (e.g., bind whole output by default, then select the package subtree). Surviving code that conditionally formats or prints the result after the first read verifies that the selection must happen before that read.

When the issue report says the crash only occurs with an option but the unbound read is unconditional, keep the same localization while noting the broader blast radius as an unresolved question: a no-option invocation would also fail, but that does not change which function contains the deleted assignment.
skill.trigger: A function reads a local variable that has no assignment anywhere in its body, often after a conspicuous blank line or immediately before an isinstance/print consumer; the call site passes no value that could bind it.

fault_subtype: deleted derivation leaves unbound local before first read

skill.title: Registry entries keyed by module path instead of object name
knowledge: Read the public registration method in full and locate every place it assigns or computes the stored map key, including both the decorator path and the direct-call path. Compare the object attribute used there (e.g. __module__, __name__, or function metadata) with the method docstring's stated contract and with consumer expectations. Both branches often share the same wrong expression, so a fix must address both.

Find the unit test exercising the registry (grep for Registry usage in tests), then read the assertions: get('SomeName') equality, duplicate-registration message text containing 'SomeName', and list(registry) containing the name. Compute what the observed key-derivation expression would store for a class defined in the test module: a module path makes all three assertions fail, while the class name makes them pass. This discriminates candidate key attributes without running the buggy code.

When localizing, do not rank downstream storage, retrieval, or iteration methods first: their checks reveal that they store/return the key verbatim and therefore only propagate the earlier derivation mistake. The duplicate-registration assertion is especially useful because its message exposes the stored key passed into the lower-level store helper.

Establish responsibility by contradiction between the method's own docstring/test contract and the actual attribute read in the key-derivation assignment; then confirm the issue's failure by tracing that stored key to the consumer's name-based lookup.
skill.trigger: Use when a registry/dict/local name-to-object map cannot be retrieved by the class/function name and enumeration reveals module strings, or when a test expects get('ClassName')/duplicate-name errors but the implementation stores module-path keys.

fault_subtype: registry key derivation uses __module__ in place of __name__

skill.title: Text-extraction normalization fuses words by deleting separators while sibling helper branches are unreachable or inverted
knowledge: Search for a normalization replacement that can emit a separator. An empty replacement can only delete whitespace runs, so if any documented example or test expects a space or newline between formerly whitespace-separated nodes, the normalizer is defective; a whitespace-only example expecting empty output explains why stripping looks locally plausible but does not excuse the line.

Read the whole normalization module rather than stopping at the first suspicious replacement, and test every helper branch for reachability and consistency with its own name, declared constants, and callers. Look for a state flag initialized false and only assigned inside the branch it gates (an identity no-op), an append gated on an empty buffer that drops non-empty merged text, and marker predicates inverted relative to declared inline/separator sets. Any such branch promotes its enclosing helper into the candidate set even when the issue only mentions disappearing whitespace.

Use per-tag contract pairs to discriminate the failing stage: inline spans should keep a single space, block elements should introduce a separator or newline, and separator tags should map to their own boundary. If the words are correct but a separator is extra or missing, rank the marker/newline-collapse/merge helpers first; if words are still fused, keep the whitespace normalizer first. Follow pointers from the test harness into the authoritative base expectations, and do not assume an unrelated test file confirms the contract.
skill.trigger: Use when extracted text from markup is missing expected spaces, line breaks, or block/inline separators, and the extraction path contains a whitespace-normalization step plus adjacent newline-collapsing, buffer-merge, or inline/block marker helpers.

skill.title: Styled wrapper opener is emptied when token styling lookup succeeds
knowledge: When a formatter emits empty or misplaced wrapper tags in one output mode, read the block that constructs and caches the per-token wrapper opener for both mode branches. If the branch assigning the empty opener is taken when the styling helper returns a truthy token-has-style result, treat that branch as inverted unless the helper contract shows the discarded result is not an attribute to emit.

Resolve the styling helper's return contract before judging the branch: locate the helper definitions and the stylesheet/class-map builder. If the helper returns a class-name key that must be looked up in a style map to produce the style attribute, a non-empty key means a styled wrapper must be built, and discarding it into the empty opener is the responsible inversion. If the helper already returns a complete attribute string, look instead at the per-line join or caller.

Inspect the per-line or per-token join that emits and closes wrapper openers around comments about avoiding empty tags. If the comment describes the condition that should take the special branch but the guard uses its negation, compare the two extend/emit paths and suspect the branches were swapped.
skill.trigger: Apply when a formatter or emitter under a mode flag produces empty or misplaced wrapper tags and uses a helper to decide whether a token has a class or inline style before constructing a span/wrapper opener.

skill.title: Whitespace boundary predicate misclassifies inline tags as block-level
knowledge: After reading the body of the issue-named whitespace/boundary predicate, grep its call sites and read the callers: if they invoke it on previous/next siblings and then remove, lstrip, or rstrip whitespace, a wrong True for an inline sibling directly produces missing spaces and exonerates downstream text/format conversion functions that only implement the verdict.

When a paired predicate exists for the opposite side of the same boundary domain, read both in one view and diff their tag tuples; an inline-content tag present only in the outside/block-boundary set is the narrowing signal for a misclassification. If the tuples match, reassign suspicion to the consumers or to a genuinely block-level branch.

Validate the tag-set asymmetry against the repository's whitespace contracts or tests for inline/nested content: if they require spaces to survive around such content, the predicate returning True for that tag is a concrete failure. Do not be steered by symptom examples whose branch is duplicated in both predicates; use the asymmetry plus consumer behavior as the discriminator.
skill.trigger: When an HTML-to-markdown or similar formatter strips surrounding whitespace based on a predicate, and the reported symptom is missing spaces around inline or nested content such as code or strong elements.

skill.title: Documented reconstruction helper returns empty output and its score/split primitives have no callers
knowledge: Read the full delegated output-producing helper before assuming a single missing input case. If its docstring or leading comment promises a complete reconstruction but the body only initializes empty result values and returns, with no branch, recursion, or call to the primitives it is documented to use, treat the entire reconstruction as absent rather than only the zero-length base case.

Grep the module for call sites of the helper's scoring/split primitives. If those primitives have zero callers while the output-producing helper is called only from the public operation, the primitives are orphaned supplies and the missing text-producing consumer is the helper; rank the helper first and the wrapper second, because the wrapper may correctly normalize or propagate whatever the helper returns.

When establishing what the absent reconstruction must emit, inspect the sibling dynamic-programming alignment that still works and reuse its gap-character insertion and joined-output idiom. Use existing tests or documentation for the expected joined string format as a contract: a candidate method whose return type is only a score list or split index cannot be the gap-alignment site.

If the scoring/split primitives do have live callers and only one input-length case fails, narrow the fix to a missing branch inside the helper. If no caller exists, keep the whole reconstruction as the top-ranked responsibility and do not patch the orphaned primitives merely because they are named in the suspected path.
skill.trigger: Use when a public operation delegates to an output-producing helper whose comment/docstring promises a full reconstruction, but the observed helper body only initializes empty outputs and returns. Also use when the helper's internal scoring/split routines appear implemented but have no remaining call sites, especially if a public wrapper normalizes or post-processes the helper's output format.

fault_subtype: documented output-producing helper is an empty stub while its scoring/split primitives are orphaned

skill.title: Validator lookup table referenced before assignment in serialized-type validate
knowledge: When an UnboundLocalError names a lookup table inside a validator method, read the entire method body and adjacent sibling validators. If the table is assigned anywhere later in the body, Python treats it as function-local, so a membership check before that assignment raises on every call; a sibling that assigns the table before the membership test confirms the inverted order as the defect.

After identifying the suspect validator, confirm reachability through the type's declared attribute path: search the module for the type name in attribute declarations, read the owning element's property setter that writes a serialized value, and follow the serialization hook that invokes the validator. A write path into the validator supports the candidate; absence of any write or serialization use weakens it.

If every sibling validator in the module defines its lookup table before the check, treat the named local as supplied from elsewhere or already mutated and shift attention to the caller or machinery that produced the name rather than to the validator itself.
skill.trigger: An UnboundLocalError names a local allowed-values or lookup table inside a simple/serialized-type validator; the method's membership check appears before the table assignment in the same method body.

skill.title: Early return before operand type-dispatch branches
knowledge: When a helper's return value is dereferenced as a required operand or Condition, read the helper end-to-end before assuming the caller misresolved the predicate.
