An unconditional `return None` placed before later `isinstance` or type-dispatch branches is a dead-code/inconsistent-control-flow smell; the branches after it cannot supply the operand the caller needs.

After finding an early unconditional return, grep the helper's name to enumerate all call sites. Check whether any caller handles a None result, or whether every caller immediately treats the result as a non-null operand/Condition (for example, building a comparison or passing it into an expression constructor). If no caller tolerates None, prioritize the helper over the caller's predicate-resolution step.

Compare the unreachable branch bodies with the caller's needed operand: if the dead branch would return the non-subquery side or delegate to the enclosing predicate, that branch is likely the intended producer. If instead a live branch can return the required operand for the failing input, shift suspicion to how the caller selected the predicate, such as an ancestor lookup, rather than to the helper's early return.
skill.trigger: Optimizer or rewrite pass raises an AttributeError/None-consumption error while recovering an operand or Condition from a small helper that dispatches on predicate/expression types such as IN, ANY, ALL, or Binary.

skill.title: Shared migration writer missing guard and confirmation branches
knowledge: When a shared migration file-update helper is suspected of silently skipping expected rewrites, read its complete body and enumerate which branches exist: success-confirmation output, old-vs-new content difference, first generated-comment-line extraction, and missing-file creation. An incomplete branch set, especially no confirmation and a whole-content marker check, is direct evidence against the helper rather than its callers.

Grep the success-confirmation literal and the first-line generated-comment guard idiom in production code; if a sibling migration writer both extracts the first line and emits the confirmation after saving while the suspected helper does neither, treat that asymmetry as responsibility evidence and rank the helper first.

Read the migration integration test to extract the observable contract (per-file confirmation keyed to the target file's basename, no confirmation when the generated comment was overwritten, user content preserved), then trace which migration entry points and shared writer must produce it. The only writer missing that message is the strongest candidate.

Grep all call sites of the helper and inspect the template each caller passes; if every failing path funnels through the helper while a path that still prints confirmation uses an independent migrator, narrow to the helper and demote the callers, which merely supply correct template content.
skill.trigger: Applies when a shared migration or file-update helper is suspected of silently skipping expected rewrites and the project has integration tests asserting a success-confirmation message or preservation of user-edited content.

skill.title: History buffer reset assigns a sentinel contradicting its documented invariant
knowledge: When a tokenizer/stream shim recovers raw text for escaping but the opening delimiter is lost or corrupted, locate the class that owns the history buffer and read the reset/init method, the reader method, and the escaping consumer in one pass. Compare (a) the literal actually assigned to the buffer, (b) the sentinel promised by the reset/init or reader documentation, and (c) how the reader's result is consumed. A literal that contradicts the documented sentinel while the consumer escapes that result points to the reset/init method as the root cause.

Grep the reset/init method's call sites and confirm it fires in the tokenizer state that handles the opening delimiter. A single call site on every opening delimiter raises that producer's rank; if the call site is conditional, rare, or absent, consider the reader method or escaping consumer for an intermediate mutation instead.

If the assigned literal matches the documented invariant, redirect attention to the reader method or the escaping consumer: trace whether the recovered buffer is mutated, overwritten, or skipped between retrieval and escaping before ranking the reset/init assignment.

Before accepting an empty grep as evidence that a producer or call site is absent, check whether the pattern contains regex-only syntax and re-run with regex mode. An empty literal-mode result for a multi-alternative pattern does not mean the searched symbol or its call site is unreachable.
skill.trigger: When raw-text recovery or escaping around an opening delimiter is wrong and a tokenizer/stream shim maintains a history buffer, inspect the reset/init assignment, the documented sentinel, and the consumer that escapes the recovered text.

skill.title: Closing-tag serializer uses reversed percent-format operands
knowledge: For a format-argument TypeError during close-tag emission, search for percent-format sites whose right-hand operand is a quoted template (e.g. grep patterns for `% "` and `% '`). If the tag variable is on the left of `%` and the quoted template is on the right, the operands are reversed and the tag name is being used as the format string; this is the likely defect. If every percent-literal site is oriented as `"</%s>" % tag`, redirect the search to producers or mutation of the substituted tag variable.

Locate the content-type-gated closing-tag branch and read it next to the parallel opening-tag serializer in the same handler. A correctly formatted start-tag emission alongside a broken end-tag emission localizes the defect to the closing path; use symbol lookup to bind the containing definition before ranking.

After a broad content-type grep returns several `application/xhtml+xml` handling sites, discard candidates that only route or escape the type rather than serialize `</tag>`; sanitizer whitelists and content routing functions cannot themselves produce a format-string TypeError. Keep sites whose body emits a tag literal through formatting before choosing between them.

If the candidate branch contains a join or concatenation rather than a percent-format, consider a different fault pattern such as a join-content TypeError or an invalid operator in a return expression; the reversed-operand diagnosis applies only when the raising site is the format operator itself.
skill.trigger: When parsing serialized markup raises a format-argument TypeError (e.g. 'not enough arguments for format string') on a content-type-gated closing-tag path that has a parallel opening-tag serializer, inspect the closing-tag string-formatting expression and compare it with the opening-tag form.

skill.title: Constructor stores transformed input copies in Object attributes
knowledge: Inspect the constructor of the affected data class assignment by assignment: each attribute assignment should place its constructor argument into the attribute verbatim. Flag any assignment whose right-hand side transforms the argument (e.g., `self.value = value[::-1]`, `self.start_pos = (start_pos[1], start_pos[0])`, `self.prefix = prefix.upper()`). If the constructor stores arguments verbatim, the corruption must originate upstream (e.g., tokenizer or caller).

Grep the repository for the same transforms used in the assignments (e.g., `[::-1]`, tuple reversal, `.upper()`/`.lower()`). If no other occurrence provides an inverse/compensating operation, the constructor's mutation is not part of a legitimate encode/decode pair and is the root cause.

Trace the boundary between the token stream and the constructed object: locate every place that instantiates the leaf class (e.g., `convert_leaf`/`default_leaf` in parser code) and verify that raw token arguments (value, start_pos, prefix) are passed through unchanged. Also check subclass `__init__` forwarders (e.g., TypedLeaf, ErrorLeaf) for verbatim forwarding. If all construction sites forward raw arguments, the corruption must occur in the constructor itself or in the tokenizer; the constructor's store logic distinguishes the two.

Construct the simplest object directly and inspect its attributes before reading consumers: if all attributes are wrong immediately after construction, the fault is in the state assignments visible in `__init__`.
skill.trigger: When object initialization corrupts field values that should exactly mirror the constructed parameters (e.g., reversed strings, swapped coordinate tuples, uppercased text metadata) and attribute assignment lines contain visible mutations, inspect each constructor assignment against its parameter and verify whether any later transform legitimately compensates.

skill.title: Constructor stores transformed or swapped inputs in object/exception state
knowledge: Inspect each constructor assignment and every `super().__init__(...)` call: stored attributes should receive their constructor arguments verbatim, and forwarded positional arguments should match the base class's `__init__` parameter order. A visible transform in the constructor (`list(reversed(collection))`, slicing, a swapped positional pair) is the candidate fault; if construction stores and forwards verbatim, the corruption must originate upstream in the producer.

When a caller-supplied collection appears reordered, read the creation/raise site and all consumers before ranking them. If the producer builds items in natural source order and consumers iterate the stored collection without a compensating reversal, the constructor is the only place the reorder can be introduced; if either side transforms order, redirect the candidate ranking there.

Grep the package for the same transform (e.g., `list(reversed`, `[::-1]`, tuple swapping). If the constructor is the only such site, the reorder is localized to it; if other sites also transform, widen the candidate set and verify whether any of them provides a legitimate inverse operation.

Read a contract test or existing assertion governing the constructed object's attributes and treat its expected order and values as the specification; a test that preserves producer order while the constructor reverses it confirms the constructor as the defect. Verify identifiers in the issue text or MCVE against the actual source field names, since an issue may use nonexistent keywords and mislead the search.
skill.trigger: When object or exception construction corrupts field values that should mirror the construction parameters (reversed collections, swapped positional arguments forwarded to a base initializer, uppercased or reformatted text metadata) and the constructor assignment or super-init lines contain visible mutations.

skill.title: Dead context-manager import reveals missing scope in recursive sublist processing
knowledge: When the issue names a special multi-word keyword branch as broken, first read that branch's predicate and value assignment in the source; if it already matches the multi-word keyword and assigns the intended value, demote the named branch and search elsewhere rather than treating the issue wording as ground truth.

Reconcile imports against actual uses in the module: if a context manager or helper intended to adjust indentation or offset is imported but never invoked anywhere in this module, treat the dead import as a strong clue that a scope applying that adjustment was removed; if the helper is used elsewhere in the module, this inference does not apply.

Identify the recursive path that processes sub-components after the statement is split on keywords. The keyword-splitting routine only partitions tokens; the recursion over each split clause's token lists is the candidate site where a per-clause offset or indent context should be entered, so rank that recursion above the keyword-matching branch when it lacks the context scope.

Use the expected formatted output or test contract to derive the required sub-component indent or offset, then check whether the current width/offset formula can produce it without entering the missing context. If the target value is reachable only through that context, the function owning the recursion is the responsible site.
skill.trigger: Use when a formatter or pretty-printer fails to align sub-components of multi-word keyword clauses and the issue or suspected path names the keyword-matching branch as the broken special case.

skill.title: Input validator silently accepts invalid values
knowledge: Read the validator body and compare its predicates against the contract stated by its docstring/example and existing module tests. If a boundary uses a one-sided comparison where the contract requires an exact length or shape, treat that predicate as a primary candidate line.

For value-conversion validators, inspect the exact substring or representation passed to the conversion. A slice that drops one more character than intended can let overlong invalid values pass by converting only a valid tail; pair this with the exception handler, because suppressing a conversion error rather than raising makes non-convertible values silent no-ops.

In every invalid-input branch, verify that an error is actually raised. A branch that constructs an exception but only returns, calls, or drops it never propagates. When several validators in the same file share similar guard/exception structure, inspect each independently for the same inversion, wrong slice, or suppressed raise.

Use existing tests to rank candidates: map each failing accept/reject case to the specific predicate, conversion, or raise line in the validator body, while still-valid cases confirm the defect is local rather than a wholesale reimplementation. If predicate, conversion, and raise are all correct, redirect to callers instead of editing the validator.
skill.trigger: Use when an input-checking callable (attr validator, guard, predicate, or list/shape checker) is reported not to raise for invalid values, especially when multiple validators in one module share guard/exception patterns and existing tests specify the accept/reject contract.

skill.title: Optional-dependency predicate guard and fallback inversion
knowledge: For a Boolean predicate, read the full body and map every return path to the condition that reaches it: which path runs when the optional dependency is present, and what default runs when it is absent or lacks the delegated attribute. If the dependency-present path returns the negative result while the absent-dependency fallback returns the positive result, treat the predicate's own availability guard and fallback as primary candidates rather than a caller that ignores the Boolean.

Use the docstring, contract, and delegation target as authority: if the predicate is supposed to delegate the real check when the dependency is available and otherwise return a definite negative, then an absent-dependency fallback that claims the positive property without evidence, or a present-dependency path that suppresses the delegated check, strongly indicates inverted branching inside the predicate. Verify comments and apparently intact consumers against the actual path rather than assuming they prove correctness.

Search the repository for tests or consumers that pin the expected Boolean, then read the surrounding test rather than the isolated assertion: check whether it imports the optional dependency and builds its argument with that dependency's real decorator or API. A test expecting the positive result for a genuine dependency-backed object while the problem describes a negative result for the absent dependency demonstrates that both directions are wrong, so require repair of both the availability guard and the fallback default. If no such pin exists, re-rank callers or setup paths as alternative candidates.
skill.trigger: A Boolean predicate reports a property of its argument while conditionally delegating to an optional dependency or module, and provides a fallback when that dependency is absent or lacks the required attribute; the reported result is wrong for the dependency-absent case or conflicts with the dependency-present path.

fault_subtype: optional-dependency boolean predicate with inverted availability guard and fallback default

skill.title: User-facing callable forwards captured arguments incorrectly to bound internal handler
knowledge: Before judging the wrapper's call line, trace what its delegation target is bound to: search the delegating attribute or field in the module where the wrapper is created, locate assignments in the setup or context-manager path, and read the callee definitions there.

Compare the wrapper's forwarding shape against every reachable implementation the delegation target can bind: if every concrete handler accepts only zero or one positional argument, passing the args tuple and kwargs dict as two positional arguments is the defect; if a handler accepts arbitrary positional and keyword arguments, the wrapper is likely correct and the downstream handler should be inspected.

Establish the public call contract from tests, examples, or call sites: a wrapper invoked with zero or one positional argument across relevant configuration variants strongly supports the expected shape, so rank the forwarding wrapper over its handlers and configuration options.

Exclude intentional raises and unreachable siblings: if a related callable raises a deliberate warning or error by design, or if a sibling mismatch has no reachable caller or consumer, it should not outrank the wrapper whose forwarding line violates the established contract.
skill.trigger: A TypeError is raised whenever a user-facing wrapper callable is invoked, with or without arguments, across configuration variants, and the wrapper delegates to an internal handler bound elsewhere.

skill.title: Helper-local name read before assignment after return relocation
knowledge: Read the entire issue-named helper body and enumerate every read and assignment of the reported local in textual order. If the first read or return precedes every assignment, Python treats the name as local and the failure is unconditional, so rank that helper as responsible and stop caller tracing.

Cross-check whether the consuming return that should use the assigned value is missing from the end of the helper or has been relocated to the top. A top return reading the unassigned local plus no reachable final return localizes the defect to misplaced control flow inside the helper rather than to an uninitialized producer elsewhere.

Exclude a delegated callee only by reading it: if it merely indexes or transforms its argument and assigns nothing that feeds back into the reported local, it is a pure consumer and should be removed from the candidate set. If instead some branch assigns the local before the failing read, treat the failure as input-dependent and inspect callers or intervening control flow to find the path to the unassigned branch.
Do not retain nearby helper names as candidates on proximity alone; require an actual call or data-flow relationship to the reported local.
skill.trigger: An UnboundLocalError names a local variable in a specific normalization or validation helper, and the traceback points at a return near the top of that helper rather than at a caller.

skill.title: Hard-coded output-head activation missing constructor option
knowledge: Open the candidate network constructor and line-match every module, layer, and activation it builds against its signature parameters and docstring entries. If the output/classification head ends in an unconditional fixed activation while the signature and documentation expose no way to vary it, rank that constructor as the primary localization target; treat the consuming forward method as secondary unless it must branch on the new option.

When searching for the missing option, do not treat an empty alternation or class-name grep as evidence of absence: re-run each token separately or with regex enabled, and grep tests/callers for the expected option or feature name. If a test or caller constructs the class with an option the constructor cannot accept, that contract fixes the parameter name and semantics and promotes the constructor signature as the repair site.

After finding the hard-coded terminal activation, grep the construction pattern across sibling networks to decide whether it is a local one-off or a shared convention. If the same pattern appears only in the suspect class and other hits have different semantics, such as detection heads, attention layers, or internal activations, keep the repair in this constructor rather than widening to a shared base, config, or utility.

Compare the suspect output head against other classification models in the package: if peers return raw logits and only the suspect one applies a fixed terminal activation, prefer a local constructor option over changing shared infrastructure or all callers.
skill.trigger: A network constructor builds an output/classification head with an unconditional fixed terminal activation, but its signature and docstring expose no parameter to make that activation optional or configurable, and callers or tests may expect such an option.

skill.title: Sibling option missing-file guard severity and message divergence
knowledge: When a report claims two sibling options for the same resource produce inconsistent missing-file errors, do not trust the quoted message strings; read the function that handles both options and tabulate every missing-file guard's option, condition, severity (raise vs warn/continue), and message. A raise-vs-warn divergence in those parallel branches is the localization target.

Grep the repository for the exact message text quoted in the report. If it matches only tests and no production source, treat the test as the expected contract and locate the producer by tracing each option definition to the shared function they are passed into, not by searching the message string.

Read the test covering the broken option path; if it only constrains one option, search for a paired test naming the sibling option or missing-file case. A paired test expecting the same exception/error for both options confirms the shared guard function and rules out a message-only defect.

Confirm upstream option plumbing routes both sibling options into that shared function and that downstream error rendering prints the exception text verbatim; if so, severity and wording responsibility stays inside the shared guard function rather than the option parser or renderer.
skill.trigger: A report claims two sibling CLI options for the same resource (e.g., primary config vs append/extra config) handle a missing file inconsistently, and the suspected path is a shared loader/validator that receives both options.

skill.title: String sentinel default reaches numeric comparison without normalization
knowledge: Treat the exception's operand types as the primary constraint: for a str-vs-int ordering TypeError in the failing function's default-argument path, map every comparison operator and record what type each operand receives from the signature defaults and local assignments; the candidate is the comparison where one side can be the string default or sentinel and the other is numeric.

Read from the signature default to that numeric comparison and look for the normalization branch that maps the sentinel to a number; if the comparison is reached without an intervening equality guard or conversion, rank the comparison as the fault site. If such normalization exists, the string is converted first and the TypeError should be sought elsewhere on the path.

Do not let the report's causal story or dependency/version label select the site: a version-style comparison with string operands on both sides cannot produce the reported str-vs-int error, and a dependency-version read that is only stored or read cannot raise this exception.

Before retaining an adjacent boundary or downstream consumer, open its body and confirm it contains the comparison or calculation that can raise the reported error; if it only reads or stores the value, keep the producer's constructor/default path as the likely fault.
skill.trigger: TypeError such as "'<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'" occurs during construction or default invocation, while the report attributes the failure to dependency/version logic or another named feature; suspect a symbolic string default/sentinel used later in a numeric check.

skill.title: Formatter indexes the wrong lookup table and drops the reset terminator
knowledge: After grep on the formatter name fixes the read location, read the page containing the function body and the module-level lookup tables together. Enumerate each table's key convention (bare names versus prefixed names) and match every subscript inside the formatter to the table whose namespace it uses; a subscript that crosses namespaces (a bare name used to index the highlight table, or a prefixed name used to index the color table) is the reported KeyError and confirms the formatter as the fault site rather than a caller-supplied key or table mutation.

On the same page, list the module's reset/terminator and other output constants, then check the formatter's output tail: if it appends an empty string or literal while a defined reset constant exists nearby, that is a second defect in the same function and explains the missing escape wrapper. Cross-check by grepping the tests for the formatter, which typically pin a concrete expected escape sequence and sweep every table key through the function.

When the caller binds keywords in an order that looks swapped, read the callee body on the same page before promoting the callee: if its early checks implement the documented suppress/force contract and only the argument binding at the call site is inverted, keep the fault inside the caller and drop the callee. Also note that a swapped binding is inert when both options sit at their defaults, so it cannot explain a default-path plain-output symptom; that symptom comes from the ordinary early return.

While the page is open for the primary candidate, scan sibling definitions for error paths that return a value instead of raising (e.g. an attribute hook returning a message where AttributeError is expected). Grep the repository and tests for consumers of that contract: if a test asserts the deprecation/attribute behavior, the sibling belongs in the candidate set even though it does not explain the reported symptom; if nothing references it anywhere, it is unreachable and can remain excluded.
skill.trigger: A formatting or dispatch function returns unwrapped/plain output and/or raises KeyError for valid style names, while the module defines multiple keyed lookup tables with disjoint key conventions (e.g. bare color names versus prefixed highlight names) and a named reset/terminator constant.

fault_subtype: wrong lookup-table key namespace in style/option dispatch with missing output terminator

skill.title: Audit every branch of a derived-value factory against consumer sentinel and scheduling semantics
knowledge: When a derived timing or relative value is reported as miscalculated, read the entire factory/conversion function, not only the branch named in the issue. Compare every returned branch against its documented parameter contract: one parameter value may mean 'disable/no-op', while another must be computed from the current clock. A branch violating that contract is a separate candidate even if another branch already contains the reported arithmetic error.

For each candidate branch, identify what sentinel or concrete value the downstream consumer expects and how the consumer branches on it: sentinel may map to no-op/disable, a past absolute value to immediate fire, and a future value to schedule-at-deadline. If a branch feeds a concrete clock value where the consumer's sentinel guard expects the sentinel, include that branch in the defect set. If consumers branch consistently, rank the producer/factory rather than the consumers.

To distinguish an arithmetic/sign fault, compute whether the produced value is before or after the current clock and which consumer scheduling path it selects; a past deadline selecting the immediate-fire path explains premature timeout. Treat docstrings and comments as evidence to verify against actual consumer reads, and use tests only as later corroboration when the contract is already visible in source.
skill.trigger: A report alleges a relative delay or derived value is miscalculated by a factory that converts it into an absolute/scheduled value; the issue names one arithmetic branch, but the factory or converter has multiple branches, including a disabling or sentinel case.

skill.title: Unbound local from deleted derivation block
knowledge: When a NameError names a local inside the function under inspection, read the whole function from entry to that first read, listing every write to that name, then grep the file for the assignment pattern. If the only writers are in sibling methods and a blank line or code-removal gap sits immediately before the read, the fault is a missing initialization block on all paths, not a package-specific branch or wrong caller.

Read the call site to confirm the printed value is not supplied by the caller; then read the parametrized expected-output tests around the feature. No-package and package-given cases that expect, respectively, the whole object and a dotted subtree/scalar reveal the required derivation (e.g., bind whole output by default, then select the package subtree). Surviving code that conditionally formats or prints the result after the first read verifies that the selection must happen before that read.

When the issue report says the crash only occurs with an option but the unbound read is unconditional, keep the same localization while noting the broader blast radius as an unresolved question: a no-option invocation would also fail, but that does not change which function contains the deleted assignment.
skill.trigger: A function reads a local variable that has no assignment anywhere in its body, often after a conspicuous blank line or immediately before an isinstance/print consumer; the call site passes no value that could bind it.

fault_subtype: deleted derivation leaves unbound local before first read

skill.title: Unbound returned output buffer from deleted derivation block
knowledge: When a function's return or first read uses a bare identifier with no evident binding, read the whole body and list every assignment target; then grep the file for that identifier and classify each hit as a write (`name =`, `name[...] =`, `for name in`, augmented `+=`) versus a read (return operand, tuple-unpack on RHS, indexing or attribute access). Only reads inside the owning function, while a sibling accumulator is written every iteration, identifies a deleted output-buffer initialization/fill; if any occurrence is a write, switch to path/branch or wrong-consumer analysis.

Check the parallel accumulator for asymmetry: if it is initialized from the first value and updated inside every loop step, but the returned identifier has no matching `identifier[...] =` write, rank the returning kernel as the producer. The empty or blank gap immediately before the return is the removed derivation block, and the returned buffer's initialization/fill is the deleted code.

Do not stop ranking at the public method named in the issue: if its body only copies parameters and constructs a helper or state object, follow the constructed type to its compute method and kernel call. Treat a state method that unpacks the kernel result and indexes it as propagation, not as the producing function, and confirm at the call site that the caller supplies no value that could bind the returned name.
skill.trigger: A computation kernel's terminal return exposes a bare output-buffer identifier that has no assignment in the function body, while a parallel accumulator is written every iteration; the public entry point may only construct or forward state and a state method may only unpack/index the kernel result.

fault_subtype: deleted derivation leaves unbound local before first read

skill.title: Missing producer assignments in a specialization override
knowledge: When an undefined-local failure points at an override/specialization that also advertises super().method(...) fallbacks, read the entire override body and check every name it reads for an assignment on a path reaching that read. Missing-producer signals include a name read in fast-path arithmetic but never assigned, a flag initialized to a constant and never reassigned, a buffer bound only in the complementary scalar/array branch, and a branch whose body is only pass; the reported traceback name need not be the first unbound name on every path.

To prove the name has no producer outside the suspect function, search the identifier in regex or whole-word mode and sanity-check the result: it must find the reads/writes already seen in the target file and report any external assignment. A zero match for a name just read in the target file means the search mode is wrong; an external assignment would redirect to import/shadowing or another producer instead.

Read the base/reference implementation and the subclass contract test before blaming callers. If the base already implements the operation by delegation and the override adds branch fallbacks plus scalar-versus-array return-type expectations, the override is meant to be self-contained; a missing producer in its body is the cause, and any surviving write-once flag is contract-bearing rather than dead. Redirect to callers or dtype guards only if the base is the sole implementation or the override fully delegates.

Use the orphaned consumers to infer the deleted producer shape and rank patch sites: the write-once flag needs the missing branch assignment, the buffer read in arithmetic needs the conversion/assignment that feeds it, and the result accumulator needs the computation that previously bound it. Confirming that re-adding exactly those statements repairs every orphaned read is stronger evidence than the reported NameError name alone.
skill.trigger: Use when a NameError or undefined-local failure points into an override or fast-path specialization that reads local flags, buffers, or result accumulators with no reachable producer, especially when the method also advertises super().method(...) fallbacks.

skill.title: Swapped single/many conversion branch shapes
knowledge: When a converter's output shape is wrong for exactly one mode, inspect the converter method's mode conditional and compare each branch's returned container shape against the docstring and the existing per-branch test assertions; an inverted branch inside that method is the fault locus, not the dispatch layer.

Grep the converter name to locate its test class/assertions, then verify each mode against expected shapes; if the body's mode conditional inverts the observable per-mode output, rank the method body and preserve the correct branch as the contract.

If a direct symbol read fails while reading a method body from a mid-file page without its class header, treat the identity as unresolved: run symbol lookup on the bare method name or grep class declarations in that file, and do not infer the enclosing class from the module filename.

Treat docstrings and apparently intact consumers as contracts to verify against actual branch returns; when the observed branch output conflicts with the stated single/many semantics, the converter body is the candidate to rank.
skill.trigger: A field-to-schema converter with a single vs many/list mode emits the opposite container shape for at least one mode, while its docstring or tests describe the expected per-mode shape.

skill.title: Truncated annotation-classification dispatch leaves downstream consumers with unproduced shape data
knowledge: When a report names several annotation types that now fail together, read the full body of the central annotation-classification routine and enumerate its actual discriminants. Then grep the module for each reported construct; any reported construct that never appears as a discriminant, or appears only as an import, indicates a deleted classification branch and makes that routine the primary candidate over downstream validators or schema builders.

Build explicit producer/consumer pairs for the classifier's outputs: grep all assignments to the shape/classification constant and to the key-field/inner-type attribute, then grep all downstream reads of those names. If downstream code reads shape or key-field values that no reachable assignment writes, the missing writer belongs in the annotation classifier; rank it above the consumers that surface the failure.

Treat unused imports and absent error strings as evidence of removed dispatch code: grep each typing/helper name imported by the classifier module and count uses outside the import line, and grep the report's user-visible error text. Helpers used only on import lines plus no source occurrence of the error string indicate a removed dispatch chain and its fallback raise, pointing to the classifier as the defect site.

Confirm the invocation order (setup/preparation, then annotation classification, then validator population/schema consumers) before assigning blame. An error surfaced in a downstream consumer should be reassigned to the classifier when that consumer expects classification data that was never produced.
skill.trigger: Use when multiple previously supported annotation types fail together during model or field construction, and the suspected path is the routine that classifies annotations into validation shapes.

skill.title: Swapped arguments between paired bound formatters
knowledge: When a serializer reports that an int lacks an attribute that belongs to the definition object, read the shared range-formatting helper and note which parameter its body dereferences for that attribute; then read every caller, especially the sibling formatter for the opposite bound, and compare argument order.

Require identical argument order across sibling bound formatters: a lower-bound caller passing the definition object first and the numeric bound second, while the upper-bound caller passes the numeric bound first and the definition object second, is distinguishing evidence that the upper-bound call has the arguments swapped rather than the helper body being wrong.

Verify the contract against the definition model: if the queried attribute is a property of the definition object and not of the numeric bound, a call passing the numeric value first can produce exactly the reported AttributeError; if the attribute is available on both, continue looking elsewhere.

Check each call site individually instead of assuming the defect is duplicated: only the sibling call whose argument order diverges is responsible, and another attribute-definition path may already pass arguments correctly.
skill.trigger: A serialization or dump path raises an AttributeError such as an int lacking .minimum or .maximum while formatting a range supplied by a definition object; suspect a shared helper called by sibling lower-bound and upper-bound formatters with inconsistent argument order.

fault_subtype: Swapped arguments between paired bound formatters in serialization helper

skill.title: Property getter drops backing attribute by returning hard-coded None
knowledge: When an accessor returns a hard-coded constant, read the whole class body and check three structural invariants: the constructor assigns a private attribute from a like-named parameter, the paired setter writes that same private attribute, and a sibling property returns its own backing attribute. If all three hold, rank the accessor as dropping stored state because set-then-read cannot round-trip and the value promised by docstring or type annotation is lost.

Before ranking the accessor, test the producer hypothesis by searching construction call sites of the consumer class and reading the loader/builder that creates it. If the required value is a populated object, the accessor is discarding it; if the argument is omitted or explicitly None, redirect to the producer or loader instead.

Use a structurally identical sibling accessor in the same class or module as the intended-behavior comparator: if it uses the same backing-attribute pattern and returns that attribute while the suspect accessor returns a constant, the sibling body corroborates the missing return. Treat comments or docstrings as leads to verify against the actual accessor body.

Distinguish this from setter-polarity or constructor-assignment faults by checking whether the constructor and setter already preserve the value and only the read path drops it. When the read path is the only broken link, report the accessor or getter rather than the producer.
skill.trigger: Applicable when a property/accessor returns a constant such as None while a like-named private attribute is assigned in the constructor and written by the paired setter, especially when a sibling property returns its backing attribute.

skill.title: User-facing callable forwards captured arguments incorrectly to bound internal handler
knowledge: Before judging the wrapper's call line, trace what its delegation target is bound to: search the delegating attribute or field in the module where the wrapper is created, locate assignments in the setup or context-manager path, and read the callee definitions there.

Compare the wrapper's forwarding shape against every reachable implementation the delegation target can bind: if every concrete handler accepts only zero or one positional argument, passing the args tuple and kwargs dict as two positional arguments is the defect; if a handler accepts arbitrary positional and keyword arguments, the wrapper is likely correct and the downstream handler should be inspected.

Establish the public call contract from tests, examples, or call sites: a wrapper invoked with zero or one positional argument across relevant configuration variants strongly supports the expected shape, so rank the forwarding wrapper over its handlers and configuration options.

Exclude intentional raises and unreachable siblings: if a related callable raises a deliberate warning or error by design, or if a sibling mismatch has no reachable caller or consumer, it should not outrank the wrapper whose forwarding line violates the established contract.
skill.trigger: A TypeError is raised whenever a user-facing wrapper callable is invoked, with or without arguments, across configuration variants, and the wrapper delegates to an internal handler bound elsewhere.

skill.title: Wrapper forwards positional arguments inconsistently with internal helper's parameter contract
knowledge: Page the public wrapper's delegation line and the private helper's signature together and write out the positional mapping. If the wrapper forwards a path-builder result and a key/timeout in the reverse of the helper's declared `(path, timeout)` order, rank the wrapper call line over the helper.

Confirm the direction by reading the first use of each helper parameter: the parameter that is hashed, joined into a path, or opened is path-valued, while the parameter used as a timeout/flag is not. A default value such as None reaching the path builder's string operation explains the runtime error and pins the defect to the wrapper's forwarding line.

Establish the intended public contract from tests or call sites: if a test invokes the public method with the logical key and expects the stored value, the correct delegation must hash that key and pass the timeout separately. This contract outranks the helper's declared parameter order because callers use the public method.

When the same class has a sibling cleanup loop, reconstruct on-disk naming conventions from writer-side path builders before trusting filename transformations. A suffix slice that no writer ever adds fabricates a nonexistent path and is a separate defect to rank when that cleanup loop is in the suspected path.
skill.trigger: A public wrapper method delegates to a private same-named helper, and the reported error indicates a non-string/default value reached a path, hash, join, or open operation; a caller/callee argument-order mismatch is suspected, or the same class has a cleanup loop transforming stored filenames.

skill.title: Subclass omits a documented metadata attribute that the base defaults to falsy
knowledge: When an issue says a named registered class is missing a metadata attribute, read the full class body and enumerate its class-level assignments; if the class declares peer metadata attributes but omits the named one while sibling implementations of the same base declare it, rank that class declaration as the omission site.

Check whether the named resolution or reproduction function actually reads the missing attribute before ranking it. If the function only resolves a name/alias and instantiates without dereferencing the attribute, demote that function and search the package for the real consumer instead.

Read the base class default for the attribute and how the sole consumer accesses it. If the base supplies a falsy default and the consumer tolerates that falsy value with an else branch, the supported fault is a missing per-subclass assignment, not a removed base default or a hard consumer requirement.

Verify the registration mapping contains the class and alias before concluding the attribute omission prevented registration. If registration is present, treat the metadata omission as the defect and keep the lookup path only as the user entry point.
skill.trigger: An issue reports that a named plugin, lexer, or registered implementation class is missing a required metadata attribute and attributes a runtime failure to a lookup/instantiation path. The class is already registered and appears to define sibling metadata attributes.

skill.title: Multi-element text accessor loses inter-element separator while paired setter transforms instead of passing through
knowledge: When a text getter over multiple nodes concatenates output without expected spaces, find the single expression that combines per-element results (join, format, or concatenation) and inspect its separator literal before examining per-element extraction; an empty-string separator where contract tests expect spaces ranks this accessor as the fault site.

Read the suspect accessor's in-function docstring/doctest alongside its body and compare the treatment of each parameter; if an example shows an assigned value landing unchanged but the body applies an unexplained slice/reversal/encoding, treat the setter as an independent defect candidate and corroborate with repository round-trip tests that write then read the value.

If a higher-level wrapper appears in the symptom, read both its set and get branches for the relevant value type and identify the downstream accessor it delegates to; a wrapper that only forwards to a delegate cannot be the transformation origin, so rank the delegate's setter/getter higher.

When a per-element helper is suspected of dropping separators, inspect its signature and call site: parameters controlling intra-element block/newline normalization and iteration once per element show it cannot decide inter-element joining, leaving the join point at the caller.
skill.trigger: Use when a getter over multiple nodes returns concatenated text without expected separators, and/or a paired setter stores a transformed value while docstrings or tests describe assigning the input unchanged.

skill.title: Subclass declared without its required base class while the base import remains dangling
knowledge: Read the target class's module end-to-end and list every self.<name> referenced in its methods. If none of those names is defined in the module or installed in a local __init__, the class must obtain them through inheritance; an empty-parens declaration such as 'class SomeGrant():' is therefore a structural defect candidate.

Search for the module's imports and then grep within the module for each imported base-like name excluding its import line. A base-class symbol that occurs only in the import statement is a dangling import, strongly suggesting the base was removed from the class declaration rather than never needed.

Run a declaration-line grep over the package/directory containing sibling classes (e.g., regex '^class \w+Grant.*\(') and compare bases. If all siblings inherit the same common base while the target class appears alone with empty parens or no base, the target's declaration is the anomaly and should be ranked first.

Locate the common base class and inspect its __init__ and helper methods. If the base assigns exactly the attributes the target's body references (e.g., request_validator, token modifiers, custom validators) and defines the helper methods the target calls (e.g., default headers, grant/scope validation), the base is the missing dependency and the fix is confined to the one declaration line.

Rank the missing-base declaration itself as the primary defect; rank the target's methods that read those missing attributes as symptoms, not separate defects, because rewriting method bodies cannot supply the state the base constructor installs.

Consider the alternative that the defect is method-local only when the class already inherits the suspected base or when the referenced state/helpers are defined elsewhere in the module. The combination of empty-parens declaration, dangling base import, and sibling inheritance distinguishes missing-base from behavioral/logic bugs.

When siblings override a method that the target also defines, compare the target's method body to a sibling's only if the inheritance link is already confirmed; otherwise the inheritance defect explains method failures and further body diffing does not change fault localization.
skill.trigger: When a class body uses self.* attributes or methods that are not defined anywhere in that module and the class has no __init__, and a base-class-like name is imported but appears otherwise unused, especially when sibling classes in the same package are declared with a common base.

skill.title: Subclass declaration omits a shared capability base that peer classes still inherit
knowledge: When a symptom is a missing capability on a class type, find the base that declares that capability, then grep the base's name across the package to enumerate its subclasses and compare each peer's base tuple. Reading the module page that spans both the base declaration and the target declaration often shows the anomaly in one view: if the scoped statement peers list the base while the target lists only unrelated bases, the target's declaration is the defect and the one-line base restoration supplies the capability.

Determine what the consuming pipeline actually calls before searching for the method name quoted in the issue: grep for the pipeline's dispatch on the node (e.g., an attribute call it invokes on the object) and grep for the issue-named method definition. If no definition of the quoted name exists and the pipeline dispatches through a differently named member supplied by the base, treat the issue name as shorthand and move the candidate set to the base declaring that member; chasing the quoted name alone dead-ends.

Distinguish the removed-inheritance case from an unused-import pattern: the base may be defined in the same module as the target rather than imported, so a square symbol that appears only in an import line is a supporting signal, not a requirement. The decisive check is always the target's base tuple versus its peers'; if all statement nodes already inherit the capability base, switch to alternatives such as an earlier MRO entry shadowing the member or a genuinely method-local logic defect.

Rank the declaration as the primary defect and the target's methods that read the missing state/helpers as symptoms, since rewriting bodies cannot supply behavior the base installs. Fix scope stays on the single declaration: a derived subclass (e.g., the from-import variant inheriting the import node) is covered by the same fix unless it defines its own copy of the capability, in which case that declaration must be inspected too.
skill.trigger: When a type is reported missing a capability or method after an inheritance change, and that capability/state is not defined in the type's own module body, especially when sibling peer classes in the same package still declare a common capability base.

skill.title: Incomplete shared signature-parameter merge with asymmetric field producer
knowledge: When a generated signature omits alias-renamed fields or custom-initializer parameters, read the whole page containing the shared signature-parameter merge helper and list the names it writes versus the names it reads or branches on. A replacement computed and not stored in the result mapping, branch bodies containing only a pass, or a name read/branched on without any binding on that page indicate the helper body was truncated; prioritize this helper over helpers it calls whose return is discarded by the same loop.

Use tests that assert expected signatures as the contract. If expected signatures contain parameters declared only in a user initializer or under an alias, and the merge helper mutates a parameter object but never inserts it into the merged result, the missing store is the primary culprit. Confirm by checking whether the observed code can produce those exact expected parameters.

When the symptom covers both ordinary model and dataclass model constructors, trace each path's data argument from the signature wiring to the field-producing function; if the shared consumer is broken, also inspect the producer. In the producer's field-collection loop, check for guards and handling exercised elsewhere—skipping non-dataclass MRO bases and handling init-only versus init-disallowed fields. If the producer is asymmetric with its own documented consumers/tests, rank it alongside the shared helper, because fixing only the helper cannot restore contract-consistent signatures.
skill.trigger: When inspect.signature on model classes omits or misrepresents alias-renamed fields or parameters declared only in a custom initializer, especially when ordinary-model and dataclass-model paths share a signature builder and each supplies fields from its own producer.

skill.title: Conversion-factory builder loses specialized node selection
knowledge: When several reported conversion functions all resolve through one Parser.FUNCTIONS factory, collapse the candidate set to that factory and its nested builder, then read the body: if it stores the target kind/safety flag as inert kwargs and never branches on argument literal/string/numeric shape, treat the inner builder as the defect site rather than each registration.

For a builder that emits a generic function/identifier container, grep the dialect's generator transforms and custom *_sql methods for the specialized node classes the same function names must render from (format-bearing parse, Unix-time/scale, date/time coercion). A renderer reading format/safe/scale args whose node is never constructed by any parser builder pinpoints a producer/consumer mismatch at that builder.

Open the dialect test file at the reported function names and read cross-dialect read/write expectations, not just the round-trip string. Expectations that a conversion input becomes another dialect's format-parse or Unix-time cast require the parser to emit the corresponding specialized node; a generic node that passes only the self-round-trip is the wrong implementation.

To recover deleted branch logic, scan generated API docs for the module/symbol and grep imported helpers or predicates for import-only hits. A documented body branching on literal vs numeric vs date/time and using an otherwise-unused format helper or numeric predicate is evidence of a regression; verify the documented signature and line alignment, since docs may not always match the clean revision.
skill.trigger: When several dialect conversion functions (timestamp/date/time and TRY variants) are mapped through one parser factory whose inner builder returns a generic function/anonymous node and format-string, Unix-timestamp, or date/time coercion semantics are lost.

skill.title: Reader magic-prefix branch inverts header-retention and stream-offset state
knowledge: When initialization branches on a magic-prefix token and the prefix-present body both reassigns preserved header state and repositions the stream, decide branch polarity from the repository's authoritative implementation of the same contract instead of the issue text: grep the prefix literal and the state attribute across the whole repository (a file-scoped grep can miss the reference reader), then read that reference implementation's docstring/body and any companion is-<format> helper to see where it leaves the offset and when it returns None. If the reference keeps the header and leaves the offset just past the prefix on the prefix-present path while only the missing-prefix path rewinds/resets, the observed prefix-present body that nulls the state and seeks to an odd offset is the inverted branch and should be ranked first; if the reference also resets on the prefix-present path, suspect a shadowing getter/property over the attribute instead.

Confirm the branch is the origin rather than a downstream symptom by grepping the state attribute within the class: if this branch is the only writer, it is the whole cause; if other writers exist, widen the ranked set before committing.

For a delegating call that passes two or more same-typed positional flags, locate the callee definition (it may be printed on the same page) and align the arguments flag-by-flag with the signature, then read how the callee consumes each flag to confirm the swap changes behavior rather than being cosmetic. A nearby call that passes the same flags by keyword in the declared order is a contrast showing the positional order is a deviation, which promotes the caller from a mere downstream consumer to an independent defect site worth keeping in the ranked set.
skill.trigger: When a format reader's initialization reads a fixed header plus a magic prefix and then branches on that prefix, and the failure is that preserved header state becomes None (or the stream is left at a wrong offset) for otherwise valid input.

skill.title: Malformed definition separator attributed to preceding body
knowledge: When a report says a definition is missing or unrecognized because the separator before it is absent, read the exact def boundary before accepting the named definition as faulty. If the def occupies its own physical line at enclosing-scope indentation and its body is complete, the reported definition is structurally intact; treat the preceding body as the owner of the malformed boundary and rank it at least as high. Only rank the reported definition itself when its def line is physically merged with the prior statement or mis-indented.

Confirm boundary ownership by scanning both neighboring method bodies for whitespace-only lines and comparing each blank line's indentation with its enclosing block. A cluster of blanks whose indentation matches no enclosing level, ending at the reported junction, indicates the malformed representation was introduced into the preceding body. Zero-length blanks or blanks whose indentation matches their block do not discriminate.

Do not rely solely on the identifier named in the report. Search for it; if it has no definition, map the informal name onto the nearest real definition using structural context such as log/progress text or a body region ending at the reported junction, and include that definition in the candidate set. If tests do not exercise the named method, the source-boundary and indentation checks carry the ranking.
skill.trigger: A report claims a method/definition is missing, unrecognized, or improperly separated because a newline/blank-line boundary before it appears absent, especially when the reported definition is expected to be a separate class-level method.

skill.title: Dialect override normalizes one compound-DML clause branch while a symmetric clause branch remains a pass-through
knowledge: When a dialect-specific override is suspected of failing to normalize a subexpression, read the complete override for the compound statement node and diff each clause-kind branch against the override's docstring or stated normalization intent; if the reported clause branch contains only a pass or no mutation while a structurally symmetric sibling branch performs the same target-qualifier stripping, prioritize that empty branch as the defect site.

Before ranking a dialect override, read the shared generator method and parser path for the reported clause and check whether they emit or store the column list through a transform, dialect hook, or qualifier-stripping step; if both pass the same container through verbatim, normalization cannot live there and the search belongs in dialect-specific overrides rather than in the renderer or parser.

Verify the object the override must mutate against parser and renderer roles: confirm the clause stores the reported column list in the container the override expects, such as a tuple or list of qualified columns, and that no earlier parse representation already drops qualifiers; if the container differs or qualifiers are already gone, redirect to the parser representation or a downstream transformer instead of ranking the branch.

Use dialect wiring and dialect tests as consistency filters: grep the candidate normalization hook or statement node key in each dialect's transform map to see whether the reported failing dialects are exactly the wired ones, then read dialect test cases for the reported clause to obtain the codified before/after output; a contract test that still fails against the pass/no-mutation branch confirms the defect, while mismatched wired dialects mean other overrides remain candidates.
skill.trigger: Use when generated SQL for a dialect retains target-table qualifiers or another normalization artifact in one clause of a compound DML statement while a sibling clause kind is reported or expected to be normalized.

skill.title: Bare identifier read whose scope binds only a renamed destructured value
knowledge: When a NameError names a bare identifier, grep that identifier repo-wide and classify each hit as a read or a write: rule out modules where every read is preceded by an assignment in the same scope, and prioritize the read whose same-scope predecessors bind only a differently named value (e.g. a pop/destructuring into a variant name), with no module-level or imported definition of the name in that file. This points to an unbound-local/renamed-binding defect at that function rather than at the correctly assigned usages elsewhere.

Read the enclosing function body around the suspect read to confirm no intervening assignment, re-binding, or conditional/loop branch assigns the name before it is used; only then treat the read as unbound rather than as a value supplied from an outer scope or an earlier branch.

Find the sibling or parallel implementation that handles the same token/operation (search the same file for the shared keyword constant or the constructor call) and read it: if the sibling derives the name from the same input value with the conversion the consumer expects, the read site is missing that binding/derivation, which pins the target and its intended producer; if the sibling also leaves it unbound or binds it differently, widen the search to the callers that supply the value instead.
skill.trigger: A NameError or undefined-name report names a bare local identifier inside a handler/function branch; the input value is popped/destructured into a differently named local and no assignment to the read name is visible in that scope.

fault_subtype: bare local read with only a renamed/destructured binding in scope (unbound local from missing assignment/conversion) before first use

skill.title: Ancestry Helper Order and Subtype Operand Inversion
knowledge: For an ancestry-splitting helper, substitute a concrete leaf and walk the literal loop guard, append site, and parent assignment: distinguish leaf-to-root ordering from a guard that stops before the root; both can coexist, so describe and check the guard and any reversal/buffer step separately rather than assuming a single missing reverse.

For a subtype/containment predicate, compare the body's operand order against the function's own docstring and any grep-visible test assertion that pins the direction, then read the container's membership semantics to see which operand is the subtype; an exact operand inversion is a defect even without execution.

While a source page is loaded for any helper in the suspected path, audit every other function body on that page: the docstring should be the first statement and every return/loop name should be assigned earlier; a return before assignment or displaced docstring is a self-contained anomaly.

For such an anomalous helper, grep its name for callers and tests; if a caller sits on the issue's named symptom path (for example a CLI filter or option) and a test asserts its contract, promote it into the ranked candidate set alongside the issue-named functions.
skill.trigger: When helper functions traverse a node/parent ancestry chain or test a subtype/containment relation and symptoms report reversed order or inverted subtype results, especially when the loaded source page shows multiple helper bodies with their own docstrings or contracts.

skill.title: Deleted public registry/collection methods with orphan internal helper and unused collaborator import
knowledge: When a collection/registry class is reported to be missing methods, read the complete class body and module tail, then inventory every private helper and module-level import; if a helper is referenced nowhere except its definition while its docstring matches what failing callers need, and an imported collaborator appears only on its import line, treat both as deletion residue and rank the class as the defect site rather than its callers.

Grep each suspected public member name and each orphan helper separately across the repository. Absence of any definition for the public member, combined with the helper having no call sites, indicates a removed public member rather than a rename or caller misuse; a live caller invoking the missing member then establishes the required signature, argument order, and return shape.

Before committing to the class, read the class's existing unit tests and fixtures: tests that call members absent from source, and fixtures naming expected collaborators and their operations, define the intended public API surface, return type, and serializer behavior, and help reject rename or caller-side explanations.

Check production consumers of each missing accessor, especially both keyed-lookup and serialization/XML accessors in this pattern; if consumers require both forms, expect to restore both public members instead of treating either as vestigial dead code.
skill.trigger: A bug report claims a collection/registry class is missing required methods or properties, such as keyed lookup or serialization/XML accessors, while callers or tests still reference them.

skill.title: Mapping override field-value corruption
knowledge: When a returned introspection or serialization mapping is reported to have swapped, polarity-inverted, or numerically offset fields, read the full mapping-construction body and compare every output key with the attribute expression on its right-hand side; a mismatched sibling attribute, boolean negation, or arithmetic offset is direct causal evidence, and nearby source comments marking changed values reinforce it.

Read the parent mapping implementation and enumerate its keys: if the affected keys are absent there and the override adds them right after calling the parent builder, rank that override first; if the parent already emits those keys, consider the parent or a later mutation instead of assuming the override.

Locate the contract test or documented expected mapping and compare expected per-key values with the override's assignments; expectations that directly contradict the reported swap, inversion, or offset disambiguate among candidate overrides and confirm which builder owns the corruption.

If a symbol search returns zero matches for a symbol already seen through symbol lookup or file reading, treat the empty result as a tool or scope artifact rather than evidence of absence; rerun with and without an explicit source glob and prefer reproducible non-zero hits, then follow them to tests or docs that carry expected values.
skill.trigger: Applies when a report says an introspection or serialization mapping returned by a subclass override has swapped, polarity-inverted, or arithmetic-offset field values, especially when the parent implementation does not emit the affected keys.

skill.title: Container string override uses unexpected delimiters, separator, and repr-per-item rendering
knowledge: Grep the module that defines the container class named in the symptom for `def __str__` and `__repr__ =`, then read any override body and mechanically compare it against the three axes the report specifies: delimiter characters, item separator, and per-item renderer (str vs repr). A body that brackets with unexpected characters, joins with a comma separator, and calls repr() on every item while the expected format concatenates str(item) inside different delimiters is the localized defect; the byte-for-byte match between its emitted format and the reported 'actual' output confirms it.

After finding the override, read the class's own class statement to get its exact base, then read that base and check whether it defines the string method. If the base defines none, the observed output cannot come from inheritance and must be this explicit override, which raises its rank. The class's own __repr__ (returning only a length/summary form) cannot emit item contents and should not be ranked when the symptom shows item contents.

A sibling class in another module may already implement the expected format (e.g., square brackets with comma-joined lines), and a grep will surface it as a tempting target. Do not rank it before verifying reachability: if the affected class's actual base defines no string method, the sibling is not an ancestor and must be removed from the candidate set. Note that grep output alone can mislabel such a sibling match as the base-class implementation, so confirm the method's owning class by reading the file rather than trusting the search-hit label.

The expected format is often stated only in the issue text; treat that as the contract for the delimiter/separator/renderer comparison, and if tests are available read them to confirm the expected string rather than inferring it.
skill.trigger: A collection/container object's textual representation (str/repr) changed unexpectedly, showing different delimiters, item separators, or per-item rendering than the expected format described in the report.

skill.title: Filter excludes all valid items because it checks a key or attribute that valid inputs never carry
knowledge: Reproduce the routine through its public entry point on a minimal input that should produce output, and observe whether the result is empty, incomplete, or contains wrong items; an empty result from a valid input is the first sign of an over-restrictive filter.

Trace the public entry into the filtering loop or helper that decides which items are included, and inspect the guard condition against the actual structure of the input items; a guard that checks a key or attribute that valid items never carry will skip every item.

Use the routine's own docstring or examples as an executable specification: walk the documented input through the guard by hand and count the produced items; if the count contradicts the documented output, the guard is the fault location.

Compare the suspected filter against a reference implementation or equivalent helper that performs the same transformation without the extra guard; if the reference includes all items and the filter excludes them, the guard is responsible.

Inspect the test fixtures or representative inputs to confirm which keys or attributes they actually carry; if the guard's required key is absent from all valid inputs, the guard is unconditionally false and the filter is broken.

When the filter checks a key that is only sometimes present, verify whether the absence should mean 'include' or 'exclude' by consulting the documented contract and the reference implementation, not by assuming the guard's intent.
skill.trigger: Use when an expansion, discovery, or conversion routine returns an empty or unexpectedly incomplete result because a filter condition tests a key, attribute, or path form that the valid inputs do not actually possess (e.g., missing metadata key, wrong path representation, or absent attribute).

skill.title: Capability predicate excludes valid items by probing the wrong attribute or inverting success polarity
knowledge: Open the gating predicate together with the transform it gates; compare the predicate's documented contract with the exact attribute string it probes and whether it returns success or failure on a successful lookup. If the predicate probes a different protocol attribute than the transform installs, or returns false on successful lookup, rank the predicate as the fault and treat the transform and registration as downstream consumers.

Use repository-wide protocol evidence to confirm the expected attribute: grep sibling transforms/helpers and tests for the capability protocol; if the established convention and test expectations assert that capability-bearing items expose a particular attribute, use that as the reference for deciding whether the predicate checks the right thing. Treat in-code comments claiming a regression as hypotheses to verify against this attribute-symmetry check.

When the guard tests a key or attribute that only some valid items carry, derive the absence semantics from the documented contract and test expectations, not from the guard's apparent intent; a mismatch between 'absent means include' and 'absent means exclude' changes which candidates to rank.
skill.trigger: Use when an expansion, transform-registration, or capability-gating predicate/filter excludes valid items because it checks the wrong key or protocol attribute or has an inverted success result, especially when a downstream transform/registration is meant to supply the attribute the predicate verifies.

skill.title: Emitter output contradicts its paired in-file parser contract
knowledge: When a serialization layer has multiple per-consumer formatters and the corresponding parser for each consumer is embedded in the same source file, treat the embedded parser as the wire contract. For each candidate formatter, read its paired parser first, note the exact field order and separators the parser splits on, then hand-feed representative items with and without help through the formatter and parse the resulting string with that parser. A formatter that disagrees only with its own parser is thereby identified directly from source reading.

If a direct grep for the suspected formatter method name in tests returns nothing, search using the vocabulary of the bug symptom instead of the internal method name and read the parametrized end-to-end test. Its exact expected output strings, including both item-with-help and item-without-help cases, are the wire contract at emitted-text granularity. Compute what each formatter would emit for those same items and compare: each mismatch ranks a formatter, while the matching siblings are confirmed uninvolved in one read.

A generic base pipeline that only joins or dispatches formatter output, with no shared field construction, is evidence that the corruptions are local expressions inside each per-consumer formatter. When every variant is wrong only against its own paired parser and the common path is intact, rank the per-variant formatter methods rather than searching for one shared root cause.

After isolating the failing formatters, continue auditing the rest of that file's producer/parser boundary, especially the earlier stage that decides which items are passed to the formatters. Read predicates for contradictory negations, duplicated calls whose loop scopes are disjoint, or reversed iteration. Such discrepancies localize corruption in a selection-stage function even if the visible test matrix does not exercise that path, making it a co-responsible candidate to rank or mention beside the formatters.
skill.trigger: Use when multiple per-consumer serializers in one source file feed consumer-specific parsers embedded in the same file (for example shell source templates), and symptoms are consumer-specific: wrong field order, wrong separator, or a help/placeholder branch that produces no usable completion. Also useful more broadly when candidate code contains a producer/consumer wire format and tests may pin the exact serialized text.

skill.title: One-sided byte transform breaks paired serializer/deserializer identity round-trip
knowledge: For paired serializer/deserializer functions in one file, read both together and identify the exact field order the parser expects from its first reads (header/magic/checksum/payload) and each side's byte-level transforms. An in-place transform on only the consuming side (reversing, reordering, re-encoding) desynchronizes fixed-order reads even when the parser logic is otherwise correct.

Grep repository-wide for the suspicious transform when you see it only in the consumer. If no producer or caller applies a compensating transform, rank the transforming deserializer first; if a matching producer-side transform exists, the pair may be internally consistent and investigation should move to the storage/wire layer. Exclude unrelated matches that do not produce this stream.

Find the concrete caller that pairs the two methods (cache/storage dump/load) and read both directions. If the serializer output is stored byte-for-byte and later fed unchanged to the deserializer, the methods must be exact inverses; the side bearing an extra transform is the faulty endpoint, while the untransformed side and low-level parser define the contract.

When a parser resets or fails on a header comparison after being handed a transformed stream, treat that reset as a symptom of stream corruption, not as the root cause; rank the transform applier ahead of the parser unless evidence shows the parser's expected layout was changed.
skill.trigger: Use when a serializer and deserializer pair (for example dump/load or to_string/from_string) is adjacent in the source and a round-trip corrupts data, especially when the consumer applies a byte-level transform before a fixed-order parser. Also useful when a storage or cache caller passes the producer's value unchanged to the consumer.

skill.title: Consumer references a variable whose producer block is absent from the function
knowledge: Read the full function from the parameter list to the consumption seam after finding a NameError/UnboundLocalError for a consumed variable. The defect is visible when the variable appears in a comprehension or loop but is never assigned in the function body, while signature options meant to feed it (pixel-array source, codec/plugin names, keyword options, config-file/data sources) have no later use.
