A consumer line immediately following an '# Encode!' or similar comment is a strong indicator that the producer block was deleted between the validation preamble and the consumption line.

Distinguish a deleted producer from a moved or helper-supplied one by grepping the whole repository for the consumed variable and for the producer API the local documentation or test path mentions. If the variable's source occurrences are only the consumer plus documentation/test copies, and the intended producer API has no callers outside its own definition, the function containing the consumer is the responsible implementation. If any producer assignment or caller exists elsewhere, trace that reachable call path before blaming the consumer.

When the producer block is an emptied try/except whose handler matches the intended producer's exception type (e.g., a config-parse error), treat that try body as the sole candidate producer location. A bare `pass` body cannot raise the handled exception, so the handler is unreachable dead code—the seam where the assignment used to live. Corroborate by checking that the consumed variable has no assignment anywhere in the module and that the intended producer's constructor/API is imported but never called; then rank the function containing the seam and restore the construction inside that try.

Reconstruct the missing block's required behavior from documentation tracebacks and from guard strings that appear only in tests. When a documentation traceback routes from the public wrapper through this same function into the producer API, and exact messages for pre-checks appear only under test files rather than under source files, those tests specify a contract that only the deleted block implements—such as raising when required transfer/metadata fields are absent on a source-route, or bypassing those checks when an in-memory array is supplied. Comparing those contracts with the existing helper for constructing options reveals whether the deleted route prepared a source object or an array before calling the producer.
skill.trigger: A function performs its main work (encoding, config loading, etc.) by consuming a local variable after an options/validation preamble, but no statement in the function ever binds that variable and no other producer appears in the repository. Calls raise NameError, and source reading reveals an empty seam (often a try/except with a bare `pass` body) between the inputs that should feed the variable and the first consumer.

skill.title: Consumed output-key local with missing prefixing branch in a record flattener
knowledge: When a record-flattening helper reportedly keeps nested keys, inspect the full body from the per-key loop through the recursive consumer rather than stopping at the intact `isinstance(value, dict)` dispatch. Look for placeholder branch bodies (for example, `pass`) directly under a key-renaming/prefixing comment and for an output-key variable that is read downstream.

Grep the helper's own file for the output-key variable. If every occurrence inside the helper is a read and no path assigns it, the missing key-construction branch is the defect and the recursive call that consumes it is a victim, not an independent cause.

Recover the intended dot-join behavior from in-repo analogues instead of guessing: sibling flatteners that implement the same example, the helper's own doctest/expected dict, and contract tests that assert directly on the helper. Together these pin the level-0 key and the prefixed-key formula.

Because a flattened record may start as a deep copy of the input and insert the renamed key afterward, check whether the copied original key must be removed as part of full flattening; infer this from the expected output plus the copy/insert pair. Use call-site grep to confirm public wrappers delegate to this sole helper, which rules out caller-side causes before ranking the helper as the producer.
skill.trigger: A record-flattening or nested-normalization helper reportedly leaves nested dictionaries unflattened or produces incorrectly keyed dictionaries. The recursive dict dispatch may be present, but the output-key variable in its key-prefixing branch is consumed without any assignment on the reachable path, often because branch bodies were replaced with placeholders.

skill.title: Name-Keyed Removal Helper Normalization and Guard Mismatch
knowledge: At a cleanup or removal helper that pops a name-keyed entry, compare the key transformation applied before the lookup with the exact key spelling used when the same mapping is written. If writers store original mixed-case keys and the lookup lowercases or otherwise normalizes the caller argument, the pop cannot match and the defect is internal to the helper, so demote hypotheses about a caller supplying a non-string name.

Read the complete try/except body and check whether the except tuple covers every operation that can actually fail. A guard that lists unrelated exception types while omitting the exception raised by an unsatisfiable or malformed lookup is a strong sign the defect is in the helper's guard or key normalization, not in the input type stated by the issue.

When an issue blames a string method on an attribute or name, grep the format module for the bare method word and classify every hit. An escaped pattern returning nothing can be a search artifact; a plain search may reveal one true name-method call plus unrelated identifiers. Collapse the candidate set to the function containing the name-method call and read its full body.

Enumerate every call site of the suspect helper and read the surrounding functions. If all callers pass literals or values not derived from parsed input, the non-string-caller-argument theory is unsupported and the helper remains the primary candidate; if callers pass parsed data, trace that value back to where it is stored to determine whether a non-string name is actually possible.
skill.trigger: Use when a serialization or cleanup helper removes entries from a name-keyed mapping and the reported failure concerns a type or key mismatch on the name, especially when the helper normalizes the caller-supplied name and wraps the removal in an except guard.

skill.title: Positional accessor adds an unexplained constant delta to the base offset it wraps
knowledge: Read the accessor body together with its own docstring: if the body returns the wrapped base value plus a constant while the docstring promises the plain base index and offers no slice/exclusive-bound rationale for the delta, treat the added constant as the off-by-one. A body like `return base + 1` under a docstring 'the grid column index at which this element appears' exposes the defect directly.

Before blaming the accessor, verify the wrapped base's semantics from its own docstring and from uses that do not go through the accessor: if the base is documented as 0-based (e.g. 'leftmost position has offset 0') and is passed directly as a 0-based origin to indexing or consumers, the defect is the adding accessor, not the base. Only if the base itself aggregates preceding elements wrongly is the base the defect.

Compare sibling accessors built on the same base value: siblings that legitimately add a delta explain it as an exclusive bound (base + span). A lone bare constant added by one sibling while the others use the base undecorated or with an explicit span localizes the fault to that one inflated accessor.

Check consumers of the accessor: 0-based origin or index use (array indexing, min/max over spans, locating a cell by offset) confirms the accessor is inflated; a consumer that would genuinely require 1-based values is counter-evidence and should redirect the search to the base computation.
skill.trigger: A property or getter returning a position, index, or offset (row/column index, byte or element position) reports a value off by one or by a small constant relative to an underlying base value it delegates to.

skill.title: Branch or guard stub leaves a read-only local uninitialized in a nested helper
knowledge: For an UnboundLocalError or NameError, first grep the reported variable to collect every read site with file:line, then inspect the full body of the enclosing function or nested helper around the earliest read. Enumerate for each read every preceding assignment and the condition guarding it; an unconditional downstream read assigned only inside one branch whose alternative (else or fall-through) is a bare pass is a missing-initialization defect, so rank that function ahead of external callers or input-format explanations.

When the unbound read sits in a nested helper or generator, compare the read line span to the def lines you loaded. If the reads fall between an inner def and its boundary, resolve both the inner helper and the enclosing public method symbol; rank the innermost function containing the assignment-free read first because that is where the repair assignment belongs, and keep its only caller as a secondary candidate because a traceback may name the public entry point.

Cross-check a sibling guard stub: if a later statement mutates a value in a way that presupposes an initialized type right after a guard like `if <value> is None: pass`, the bare pass is strong evidence the original initializer was deleted. Grep the assignment form across the package to confirm; if it appears only in unrelated modules and not in the current module, treat that guard stub and the unbound path as one branch-dependent initialization defect.

Before attributing the failure to caller-supplied state or data structure, verify the helper's call graph: when the helper containing the unbound variable is defined and called only within the same method, including recursive self-calls, and no other module writes that local, the defect is contained in that nested function. This narrows the candidate set from any consumer of the value to the single function that owns the unbound read path.
skill.trigger: UnboundLocalError/NameError where a local variable is read unconditionally downstream but assigned only inside one branch of an if/else, or after a None/state guard whose body is a bare pass/no-op, especially inside a nested helper or generator.

fault_subtype: branch-dependent uninitialized local variable in nested helper

skill.title: Reversed collected output caused by aggregation/join inversion
knowledge: When concatenated output is reported reversed, first read the fragment-producing append/write path and confirm whether it stores fragments in call order; if it does, eliminate producers as the reversal source before ranking consumers.

Locate the aggregation/join accessor that consumes the whole accumulated sequence and inspect the join expression: a plain ordered join preserves stored order, while wrapping the sequence in reversed(), sorting, or a reverse iterator inverts the page at that aggregation point.

Search for the reversal primitive across producer and consumer paths; if it appears only in the aggregation/join accessor and not in the writers or callers, rank the aggregator as the faulty function rather than the writers or callers.

Cross-check an order-sensitive test or caller contract that writes fragments through the producer and expects the assembled result in natural reading order; a failure only when fragments are aggregated confirms the accessor is responsible, while producer-side reversal or caller misuse would redirect the inspection.
skill.trigger: A formatter, collector, or serializer returns concatenated output in reverse order while the individual write/append operations appear to produce fragments in reading order.

skill.title: Single-unit accessor returns hard-coded sentinel against documented fallback
knowledge: When a small single-unit accessor/getter returns a hard-coded sentinel in its empty/short branch while its docstring or type contract specifies a different fallback, inspect the accessor body first: compare the literal, the branch condition, and the delegate argument/index against the documented contract rather than stopping at the docstring-code mismatch.

Grep the state attribute named in the suspect branch condition across the repository and read the constructor: if that attribute is assigned nowhere and appears only inside the suspect condition, the branch cannot be evaluating real state, so treat the whole accessor body as the fault locus and search for the sibling reader the contract says it should use; if the attribute is assigned and a sibling accessor returns it while the suspect accessor returns a constant, consider the property-getter hardcoded-constant pattern instead.

Read the sibling reader that the docstring/annotation names as equivalent or as the delegate. If that reader already yields the documented fallback for the trivial case, one-line delegation to it with the one-unit length is the expected behavior; a divergent sentinel or a length/index argument that changes return type or consumes more than one unit marks the accessor as defective, and the low-level reader it delegates to should stay ranked as correct.

Confirm the consumer contract by grepping tests and call sites repo-wide, not only with a scoped symbol search; an empty scoped symbol search is a scope/pattern result, not evidence of absence. Tests/callers that wrap the result as a single bytes value or apply ord() and then consume subsequent units pin the accessor to a one-unit bytes return, ruling out candidates that return an int or over-consume.
skill.trigger: Applicable when a small accessor/getter has an empty/short branch returning a hard-coded value that differs from its docstring or type contract or from the sibling reader it claims equivalence to, especially when the branch condition names a state attribute of dubious provenance.

skill.title: Package-level scalar used where per-dependency generated state is required
knowledge: When a generated artifact should vary per dependency but the consumer template branches on one package-level scalar, start from tests that assert the generated data file and config file. Record the expected per-dependency variable and exact emitted line; if the data producer emits only dependency names and not that variable, rank the producer data template as missing the per-dependency state assignment and the consumer template as the wrong emitter.

Search the generator tree for the expected per-dependency mode token and for an existing per-dependency mode accessor. If the accessor returns the correct per-dependency value but is called only from filename or naming code, do not blame the accessor; rank the templates that must carry the value into the generated data and consume it when emitting the dependency call.

Inspect the consumer template's loop that emits the dependency call: a literal mode option selected by a package-level flag and no read of the per-dependency variable means per-dependency state never influences output. Confirm by searching for the asserted per-dependency variable across the whole generator; absence in the buggy generator but presence in an asserted test or a newer sibling implementation distinguishes the missing emission from an intact producer.

An imported mode constant that is never referenced in the data-target module is a source-only corroboration of missing emission. Use it to locate the producer, but require an asserted generated variable or a real consumer read before ranking the producer over the consumer.
skill.trigger: A generated dependency file or dependency-finding call should vary by dependency, but a single package-level flag or scalar-derived literal controls the per-dependency option; or tests assert a per-dependency variable that the generator may not emit.

skill.title: Helper-local name read before assignment after return relocation
knowledge: Read the entire issue-named helper body and enumerate every read and assignment of the reported local in textual order. If the first read or return precedes every assignment, Python treats the name as local and the failure is unconditional, so rank that helper as responsible and stop caller tracing.

Cross-check whether the consuming return that should use the assigned value is missing from the end of the helper or has been relocated to the top. A top return reading the unassigned local plus no reachable final return localizes the defect to misplaced control flow inside the helper rather than to an uninitialized producer elsewhere.

Exclude a delegated callee only by reading it: if it merely indexes or transforms its argument and assigns nothing that feeds back into the reported local, it is a pure consumer and should be removed from the candidate set. If instead some branch assigns the local before the failing read, treat the failure as input-dependent and inspect callers or intervening control flow to find the path to the unassigned branch.
Do not retain nearby helper names as candidates on proximity alone; require an actual call or data-flow relationship to the reported local.
skill.trigger: An UnboundLocalError names a local variable in a specific normalization or validation helper, and the traceback points at a return near the top of that helper rather than at a caller.

skill.title: Helper-local guard reads name before relocated assignment
knowledge: When the error names a specific local in a dialect-specific rewrite or normalization helper, grep that bare local name across sibling implementations rather than searching only the SQL token or function name; a same-shaped sibling that binds the local before its guard supplies the control ordering, and if the suspect binds it after the guard or after an unconditional return, rank the suspect helper and treat the sibling ordering as the expected repair.

Read the entire helper and enumerate reads and assignments of the reported local in textual order, including indentation to confirm the assignment belongs to this helper. If the first read precedes every assignment and the only assignment follows an unconditional return, the name is function-local and every call fails; keep the helper as the producer and stop tracing callers. If a branch assigns the local before the failing read, treat the failure as input-dependent and inspect callers or intervening branches.

Check the helper's tail and any early return: if an early return reads the unassigned local while the assignment is displaced below it, localize the defect to misplaced control flow inside the helper. If the tail delegates to a shared builder, read the delegate and exclude it only when it never binds or mutates the reported local or an argument feeding it.

Confirm that the reported function or argument corresponds to the local by inspecting the expression class argument metadata or the function-use path, and do not retain nearby helper names by proximity alone; require an actual call or data-flow relationship to the reported local.
skill.trigger: An UnboundLocalError/NameError names a local variable in a specific rewrite, normalization, or validation helper, and a guard or early return appears before any assignment of that name in the helper.

skill.title: Handler call site omits local binding for optional request parameters
knowledge: When a handler forwards local names to a callee and no assignment is visible in the handler body, grep the module for each name and classify every hit as a read or a write before ranking the callee. If all hits are reads inside the handler, prioritize the handler for a missing local binding; if an earlier assignment exists in the same function, inspect intervening branches or shadowing instead, and if the callee body itself contains undefined names, redirect to the callee.

Compare sibling operations in the same module for an analogous optional argument: if a neighboring call site validates or builds that argument through a helper or guarded block, read that helper and sibling caller as the intended producer template. The discriminating observation is a producer/helper that exists and is used by a sibling but is absent from the failing handler, which confirms a missing producer call or local binding at the failing call site rather than a callee defect.

To rule out the callee, read its full definition and verify that every identifier the caller passes is declared as a parameter or assigned locally and used consistently. A self-consistent callee with a matching parameter list demotes the callee and moves the undefined-name boundary to the caller's argument expressions; then read the request-parsing or validation helper for the missing optional parameter to infer intended fallback and exception behavior when the request omits values.
skill.trigger: Applicable when a reported NameError or unbound-local points at a backend/callee call, and the caller handler references one or more optional-parameter locals with no visible assignment, while sibling operations in the same module use a producer/validation helper for analogous parameters.

skill.title: Unreachable Neighbor Traversal from Hoisted Descent Return
knowledge: When a traversal method returns the receiver's own last descendant (or the receiver itself for a leaf) instead of the expected previous/next node, read the method body and check statement reachability: an unconditional return inside a descent loop makes every later sibling/parent traversal unreachable.

Continue the source page past the suspect method to read the adjacent opposite-direction traversal. If the mirror keeps the descent loop last (docstring, sibling/parent chain, then descent) while the suspect method hoists the descent loop and its unconditional return above the sibling/parent loop, prioritize an injected control-flow reordering inside the suspect method; if the mirror shares the broken ordering, consider index arithmetic or caller misuse instead.

When the same qualified traversal definition appears in both the working package directory and a build/output mirror, read and diff both copies statement by statement. A mirror that preserves the sane traversal ordering while the working copy scrambles it localizes the injected reordering to the working copy and exonerates callers; this discriminator applies only if the copies actually differ.

Follow search hits to the traversal method's tests and in-tree consumers to extract the expected contract. If consumers read the returned node's position and the current implementation can return the receiver (whose position differs), that observable mismatch supports the ordering fault over parsing/error-recovery or caller misuse.
skill.trigger: A tree-navigation method, especially previous/next-leaf traversal, returns the receiver's own last descendant or the receiver itself instead of the expected neighbor, often reported as an infinite loop or wrong node. Inspect for an early unconditional return in a descent loop that makes the intended sibling/parent traversal unreachable.

skill.title: Reserved-name guard predicate direction and helper resolution return mismatch
knowledge: Read the guard predicate body, then inspect each consumer rule and its tests; the required classification of representative reserved and non-reserved names determines the intended predicate direction, so do not settle direction from the function name or an untrusted inline comment alone.

Compare the predicate result for a reserved sample that consumer tests require to be rejected or ignored: if the predicate returns false for that sample, rank the predicate itself as the fault; if it returns true while consumer behavior still fails, redirect to the consumer call sites and branch conditions.

For a dotted-path/attribute-resolving helper, compare its documented contract and caller assertions with the actual getattr target and final return variable; if loop resolution applies the path to the base object, or the function returns the base object instead of the running resolved value, rank the helper above its wrappers and callers.
skill.trigger: Applicable when a validation guard for reserved/introspection-like names misclassifies fields, or a dotted-path/attribute-resolving helper returns a wrong base or intermediate object; the suspect predicate/helper is small and its intended direction or final returned value is ambiguous.

skill.title: Mode-flag display hook reads locals bound only under an enclosing guard
knowledge: When an UnboundLocalError is reported behind a boolean mode flag in a repr/display hook, grep the flag, then read the entire enclosing method from its def line to the next def/class boundary. Enumerate every local read inside the branches the flag controls and compare each read's guard with every assignment's guard; a local assigned only inside an enclosing width/size guard but read in the alternate arm is the real unbound site, so rank that method/function ahead of the delegate or caller.

Treat the reported variable and trigger as hypotheses: if the named variable has an unconditional assignment before any branch, the crash is another branch-local. Re-run the assignment-vs-read guard comparison on the other locals in the same branch, using grep to confirm their assignments sit inside the guard block while their reads sit in the else arm; also read the flag-assignment block to see which arm is reachable without the guard executing.

If the reported callable is __repr__ but the class binds __repr__ to a shared delegate, do not investigate the delegate for local-scope bugs; symbol-lookup the class's display/pretty hook, read that hook's full body, and grep the delegate name to confirm it is a generic dispatcher reused by many unrelated classes.

Determine the condition that sends execution down the crashing arm: when an outer width/size guard fails, a derived flag may become False without the guarded branch locals ever being assigned. This can invert the reporter's claim about the flag value, so the reproduction may require wide/oversized data rather than the flag being True, but localization to the hook remains unchanged.
skill.trigger: UnboundLocalError/NameError in a repr or pretty-printing hook where a boolean mode flag selects a full-detail arm versus an abbreviated arm, but locals consumed by one arm are assigned only inside an enclosing width/size guard; the reported variable or flag value may be misidentified.

fault_subtype: mode-flag branch reads locals bound only under an enclosing guard in a repr/display hook

skill.title: Handler success path hard-codes non-2xx status contrary to sibling handlers
knowledge: When a successful operation returns a non-2xx status, grep the success-return expression across sibling handler modules in the same family and compare the status literals. If peers return the success status and only the suspect handler returns a non-success literal, rank that handler's success return as the direct cause; if peers share the same non-success literal, shift suspicion to the shared base, endpoint, or token/session producer.

Read the endpoint or delegating wrapper before accepting an exception-converted error status: search it for generic exception-to-error mappings or status literals. If it only delegates and has no such fallback, the status must originate in the handler's own return value, which separates a hard-coded status from an exception path.

When a structural cause is proposed (wrong base class, missing mixin, bad registration), test it with a declaration grep over sibling modules. If the suspect declaration matches peers, drop the structural hypothesis and immediately reuse the same file set to inspect bodies, return values, and guard literals; if it differs, keep the structural candidate and inspect the base class.

For a request validator or handler method, compare its body with sibling handlers and with the wiring that registers it: check pre/post validation hook ordering, the operation-type string it compares against, and boolean or and/or guard polarity against the error it raises. A module that inverts hook order or tests a type literal inconsistent with its own registration is a stronger candidate than the shared wrapper, even when tests only assert that hooks were called.
skill.trigger: Applicable when an operation that should succeed returns an unexpected error status (for example 500 instead of 200), the suspected handler has sibling implementations for other operation types, and the endpoint/delegating wrapper is a thin pass-through.

skill.title: Shared matcher transforms the wrong operand relative to its cache key
knowledge: When a shared matching helper fails to match any registered pattern, compare the variable used as the cache key against the variable fed into the pattern compiler: if the cache is indexed by the registered pattern but the regex/transformation is built from the input value (and the match is run against the input), the wrong operand is being transformed and the helper itself is the root cause.

Confirm the helper's intended contract by grepping its definition name to find a same-named sibling in a parallel module: if the sibling transforms the registered pattern and matches against the input, the divergent operand/method in the suspect establishes the defect and collapses candidates to that single helper, making callers pass-through victims.

Check each registry caller's argument order against the helper signature: loops that already pass (input, pattern) in the declared order and merely fail to find a match are downstream consumers, not alternative root causes; only a caller that reversed the roles would compete with the helper.

Separate the public dispatch entry point that only forwards into the matcher from the matching decision itself: treat the entry point as the symptom surface and rank the matcher above it, reconsidering only if the observed failure is construction/config-time rather than 'no match found'.
skill.trigger: Filename/pattern-based lookup returns no match for every registered pattern, and a shared helper caches compiled patterns and performs the match; use before blaming the registry/dispatch callers.

fault_subtype: shared pattern matcher compiles/matches wrong operand relative to its cache key

skill.title: Deleted public registry/collection methods with orphan internal helper and unused collaborator import
knowledge: When a collection/registry class is reported to be missing methods, read the complete class body and module tail, then inventory every private helper and module-level import; if a helper is referenced nowhere except its definition while its docstring matches what failing callers need, and an imported collaborator appears only on its import line, treat both as deletion residue and rank the class as the defect site rather than its callers.

Grep each suspected public member name and each orphan helper separately across the repository. Absence of any definition for the public member, combined with the helper having no call sites, indicates a removed public member rather than a rename or caller misuse; a live caller invoking the missing member then establishes the required signature, argument order, and return shape.

Before committing to the class, read the class's existing unit tests and fixtures: tests that call members absent from source, and fixtures naming expected collaborators and their operations, define the intended public API surface, return type, and serializer behavior, and help reject rename or caller-side explanations.

Check production consumers of each missing accessor, especially both keyed-lookup and serialization/XML accessors in this pattern; if consumers require both forms, expect to restore both public members instead of treating either as vestigial dead code.
skill.trigger: A bug report claims a collection/registry class is missing required methods or properties, such as keyed lookup or serialization/XML accessors, while callers or tests still reference them.

skill.title: Deleted resolver/registry methods referenced by internal and typed external callers
knowledge: When a resolver/registry class is reported to lack methods that live callers still invoke, read its whole body and collect every `self.<name>(...)` token absent from the class and its bases; grep each absent token with regex enabled when the pattern uses alternation, because a literal search containing '|' can silently return nothing. Each unresolved token is a method-level target `Class::method`, not the class or a caller.

For each `receiver.<method>(...)` in another module or test, resolve the receiver's declared type from annotations, factories, or assignments; when the type is the suspect class and no definition exists on it or its bases, emit `Class::method` as the target. Treat the caller/test only as contract evidence for exception type, arguments, and return shape, and do not rank the caller or bare class in its place.

Search tests that construct the suspect class and assert on the resulting object; each asserted method pins a required public method target, so rank that `Class::method` rather than a production property or wrapper that forwards to it.

Inventory the class's sibling methods and module-level helpers: if a populated attribute has no corresponding resolve/accessor method while sibling variants exist, or a helper with the missing behavior's purpose has no call sites, treat these asymmetries and orphan helpers as deletion evidence and rank each distinct missing behavior (keyed lookup/membership predicate, sibling resolve variant) as a separate `Class::method` target.
skill.trigger: A resolver/registry class is reported to be missing methods that its own resolve path, external callers, or tests still reference, especially after a refactoring.

skill.title: Absent protocol or factory member inferred from counterpart asymmetry and dangling calls
knowledge: When a class exposes a teardown/protocol method but not its setup counterpart, grep the counterpart's expected protocol name and the state it consumes; if that state is initialized and consumed but never produced, treat the absent counterpart as a candidate and rank its expected qualified name beside the surviving method.

When a factory/runner or wrapper/implementation family shows all but one member paired, grep the expected missing factory or wrapper name across the repository, not just the class; a call site to a name with no definition is direct evidence of a deleted member, so rank the absent factory or wrapper with the surviving runner or implementation.

Rank inferred absent member names alongside their surviving neighbors because symbol lookup cannot return definitions that are absent; use protocol/factory symmetry and dangling references as the candidate-generation evidence rather than requiring a resolvable definition.

Confirm the missing-member hypothesis is on an executed path by reading the internal call site that invokes it or the protocol counterpart and the surrounding command flow; if the counterpart is defined elsewhere or a producer for the consumed state exists, treat the case as a rename, ordering, or mutation fault instead.
skill.trigger: A class or module shows one side of a protocol pair (e.g., teardown/exit present, setup/enter absent), a factory/runner family with one member missing, or state that is consumed by a surviving member but never produced, and symbol lookup for the expected counterpart returns no definition.

skill.title: Recovering metadata-normalization defects when the reported helper name is absent
knowledge: When the reported helper or method name has no repo-wide hit, do not treat localization as blocked or chase the stale name; grep the owner class or entity the report also names, read that class body through its construction path, and enumerate methods that read the reported input fields (docstring, class name) and write the reported output fields (description, formatted identifier). The filter should collapse to one producer whose emitted strings match the report's actual output.

Validate each reported symptom independently against source rather than accepting the report's framing: grep the anomalous appended literal alone and look for occurrences outside the producer; if only the producer line contains it, it is injected text. For an ordering claim, read the input-parsing regex and the group unpacking in the same body and compare the expected name-part order to the emitted concatenation. For a transformation-direction claim, inspect how the same markup characters are used by adjacent documentation writers to determine whether the derived plain-text field should strip or add that markup.

Confirm a candidate mutator is on the live construction path before ranking it: grep the candidate's name repo-wide to enumerate call sites, then read the caller context including its guard and ordering. A call from class construction under a name guard means the corrupted fields reach every real rule or class, so consumers that only read those fields are not alternative producers.

Prefer the single method that writes both affected metadata fields over a downstream consumer; only inspect the consumer or formatting path if the producer's outputs do not already match the report's actual output.
skill.trigger: A report complains that class or rule metadata strings are mangled (wrong quote/backtick direction, appended suffix, swapped field order) and its reproduction calls a helper or method that grep shows does not exist at the revision, while naming an owning class or construction path.

skill.title: Auto-fit/version selection ordered after compile in an incremental builder
knowledge: In the top-level build method, first read the statement order: locate where the auto-fit/version-selection call sits relative to the compile/encode calls, including any helper that invokes compilation. If fit runs after a compile path, rank the build method as cause; if fit runs before, shift attention to the fit/table lookup.

Verify that every compile path does not independently fit: read the mask-selection/encoding helper and confirm it invokes the compile routine without calling fit, and inspect the capacity/version accessor to see whether auto-fit only occurs when no capacity has been previously stored. A sticky capacity plus a compile-first ordering explains overflow after the first successful build.

Use a repeated-build contract as source evidence: if tests or spec expect capacity/version to grow on a second build, the only growth point should be the fit call in the top-level build. If that call is reachable only after compile, narrow to build-method ordering rather than the fit algorithm or compile routine.

Treat the overflow exception site as a symptom when the capacity/version was valid at the start of the build: inspect why capacity was not expanded beforehand, and prefer the top-level call ordering over the data-mapping or compile internals.
skill.trigger: When a top-level build/make operation overflows on subsequent data additions despite an automatic fit mode or unspecified capacity, and a compile/encode stage appears to run with a previously retained capacity/version. Applies to builder/encoder APIs where fit/version selection and compilation both live in the top-level build method.

skill.title: Paired composite accessor returns the wrong child end
knowledge: When adjacent accessors on a composite node denote opposite sides/operands but their bodies return the same ordered-child index, inspect the accessor whose name denotes the ending side; a right/end accessor reusing the sibling's start-index expression is self-inconsistent and becomes the primary candidate.

After finding a duplicated index expression, search consumers and tests for asserted values and token types of the suspect accessor and its sibling; assertions that require the opposite end collapse the candidate set to selecting that end and rule out returning the operator, the wrong sibling, or a child-ordering bug.

Inspect the ordered child layout for intervening operator or whitespace tokens before accepting a simple first/last index fix; if the contract expects an operand, rank the accessor that selects the side operand over candidates that index adjacent operators or whitespace.

Use class docstrings or comments only to confirm the node is a paired/comparison-like structure; when contract tests are absent, compare the suspect body against the sibling accessor and the actual child sequence rather than inferring the fix from the issue text alone.
skill.trigger: When a composite parse node exposes named side/operand accessors and one accessor returns an element from an ordered child list, especially when it appears to duplicate the opposite accessor's index expression.

skill.title: Delegating method assigns helper result but omits terminal return, yielding None
knowledge: When a method's last executable statement assigns a delegated call's output to a local variable and the next source line begins a new definition, treat the method as implicitly returning None: rank this method first and search its tail for a deleted return rather than assuming the callee failed.

Cross-check initialized-but-never-read state on the same object (configuration flags, error or failed-result collections, exception accumulators). If those fields are only assigned and never consumed by the method, hypothesize a deleted return tail that would have built and returned a conditional result from them; grep for other reads before concluding they are intentionally unused.

Inspect callers and the public API contract to pin the required return shape. A caller may unpack a tuple under a configuration flag and a bare value otherwise, so restore the matching conditional shape rather than only the local value, and use the caller's expectation to confirm the method, not its caller, is responsible.

Verify the delegated helper's terminal statement returns the populated result. If the helper ends with an explicit return, remove the helper from the candidate set and focus on the delegating method that drops or fails to forward the value; if the helper's tail is itself missing a return, shift suspicion to the helper.
skill.trigger: A wrapper or forward method delegates work to a helper, assigns the helper's output to a local variable, but callers observe None; the same object may initialize configuration or error-state fields that the method never reads.

skill.title: Copy-method local read before new-instance assignment recovered from sibling ordering
knowledge: When the report names a dunder or method and the error is UnboundLocalError for a local, grep the literal name to separate definition sites, callsites, and subclass overrides; read the complete definition body in the primary module and confirm its enclosing class before ranking it. If the reproduction uses a plain base type, down-rank overrides in subclasses/modules; if it uses that subtype, pivot to the override.

Build a definition-before-use order for the named local across the whole body: locate the first assignment and check for any earlier read. If the earliest executable statements dereference the target and a string literal/docstring is stranded after executable code, treat the body as statement-reordered; if the first read comes after assignment, shift to an intervening rebinding or branch-local binding instead.

Read the nearest analogous sibling in the same class that performs the same role with a different depth or option, such as a shallow-copy method beside a deep-copy method, and use its shared-operation order as an in-repo template: class/type resolution, new-instance creation, state attribute writes, private-state handling, return. If the sibling assigns before writes and the suspect method does not, pin the fault to the suspect method; if the sibling matches, widen to the caller or metaclass.

Inspect the caller returned by the name grep: a caller that only delegates to both the sibling and suspect methods, without writing target state itself, does not own the defect; if it performs the copy work or supplies stale state, include it as a candidate.
skill.trigger: Applicable when a copy-style method raises UnboundLocalError for a local used to hold the new instance, the body appears to contain valid operations but in the wrong order, and an adjacent same-role sibling method exists for comparison.

skill.title: Constructor stores transformed or swapped inputs in object/exception state
knowledge: Inspect each constructor assignment and every `super().__init__(...)` call: stored attributes should receive their constructor arguments verbatim, and forwarded positional arguments should match the base class's `__init__` parameter order. A visible transform in the constructor (`list(reversed(collection))`, slicing, a swapped positional pair) is the candidate fault; if construction stores and forwards verbatim, the corruption must originate upstream in the producer.

When a caller-supplied collection appears reordered, read the creation/raise site and all consumers before ranking them. If the producer builds items in natural source order and consumers iterate the stored collection without a compensating reversal, the constructor is the only place the reorder can be introduced; if either side transforms order, redirect the candidate ranking there.

Grep the package for the same transform (e.g., `list(reversed`, `[::-1]`, tuple swapping). If the constructor is the only such site, the reorder is localized to it; if other sites also transform, widen the candidate set and verify whether any of them provides a legitimate inverse operation.

Read a contract test or existing assertion governing the constructed object's attributes and treat its expected order and values as the specification; a test that preserves producer order while the constructor reverses it confirms the constructor as the defect. Verify identifiers in the issue text or MCVE against the actual source field names, since an issue may use nonexistent keywords and mislead the search.
skill.trigger: When object or exception construction corrupts field values that should mirror the construction parameters (reversed collections, swapped positional arguments forwarded to a base initializer, uppercased or reformatted text metadata) and the constructor assignment or super-init lines contain visible mutations.

skill.title: Constructor stores a transformed or inflated parameter that downstream decisions consume verbatim
knowledge: Read every constructor and `super().__init__(...)` call in the hierarchy together: verify whether the base initializer stores its argument verbatim and whether subclasses pass their value straight through. A visible arithmetic or reordering transform at a single assignment site is the candidate producer; if the later decisions are plain tests against the stored attribute, rank the assignment rather than the comparison.

Trace the stored value's consumer chain end-to-end before ranking an accessor: follow any default substitution (e.g., an accessor delegates to a helper that substitutes the attribute for `None`), then read the comparison site. Unmodified comparisons such as `elapsed >= stored` mean the threshold was already wrong at storage; if any consumer re-derives the value, widen the investigation to that site.

Contrast sibling classes in the same module: a sibling that bypasses the shared initializer and stores the raw argument verbatim is evidence that the transformed assignment is the defect, whereas siblings that also transform the value indicate intended semantics and redirect the investigation toward comparison or accessor logic.

Treat a zero-match search as absence of evidence rather than confirmation: re-scope the query (different literal, test directory, or class-level pattern) and read the contract test body directly. A test that sleeps for the requested timeout and asserts expiration discriminates stored-threshold faults: any stored value strictly greater than the requested timeout keeps the entry alive past the sleep boundary, pointing at the stored value rather than retrieval.
skill.trigger: When a stored value that governs timeouts, limits, thresholds, or ordered collections is derived from its constructor argument by a visible transform (added offset, reversal, swapped positional argument) and downstream accessors or comparisons appear unchanged.

skill.title: Recursive unique-name generator counter direction and suffix arithmetic
knowledge: In a recursive unique-name helper that appends a numeric suffix before recursing, trace the counter across the recursive call: the callee must receive a strictly larger counter, and the branch that strips a previously appended suffix must remove a length of len(str(counter)) + 1 (digits plus separator). A decrement or missing separator makes the candidate name malformed or non-convergent, so keep the helper as the primary candidate until its arithmetic matches this contract.

Compare the helper's fresh-name early return with the caller's initial counter default: if the guard requires counter > 0 but the duplicate-registration caller passes only a name (counter = 0), an absent name cannot return early on the first call. Inspect the caller's argument before assuming an outer layer supplies a nonzero counter or compensates.

Read the registry check used by the early return together with the duplicate-name contract or test: the expected sequence is base name for a free name, then base + counter for each registered collision. If the observed body cannot produce that sequence, localize to the helper rather than the registration caller.

Verify recursion convergence against registry state: each candidate produced by the helper should be tested against the registry, and recursion should stop only when a candidate is absent. If generated suffixes can repeat, move backward, or leave separator characters, the helper cannot reach a free name and its counter/suffix logic remains the fault site.
skill.trigger: A duplicate-name registration path funnels into a recursive helper that appends a numeric suffix to a base name until the result is absent from a registry, but generated names never converge to a free suffixed name.

skill.title: Cached constructor hit path skips state restoration and cache never stores built instance
knowledge: Read the component constructor end-to-end and enumerate both sides of the cache: every access to the shared cache keyed by the config identity and every assignment to the component's internal state that later hooks iterate. If the hit branch returns early without restoring that internal state, treat the constructor as the fault site before inspecting hook dispatch.

Search the whole repo for a write/store into the same cache dict, not just reads. When only a get/read exists and no corresponding put exists (or only appears in an unrelated module), the observed hit path is dead: the constructor never publishes the built instance, so cached lifecycle initialization cannot occur. The fix belongs inside that constructor: restore state on the hit path and store the newly built instance after construction.

Compare with a symmetric get/set cache elsewhere in the project. A nearby cache that performs a read paired with a write, while the suspect cache performs only a read, is strong evidence of the missing half in the suspect constructor.

Trace each construction site by the cache flag and the identity of the config object: the first construction may be deliberately uncached and must populate the cache for a later default-cached construction. If the uncached call has no store and the later call has no hit, the later lifecycle setup rebuilds instead of reusing state; callers selecting cache flags and hook dispatchers are consumers, not the fix site.
skill.trigger: Lifecycle hooks are skipped, duplicated, or initialized inconsistently when the component is built from a config that a cache is meant to reuse; the constructor consults a cache keyed by config identity.

skill.title: Configured module contradicts its declared construction contract
knowledge: Read the full module definition and compare each constructor's docstring/parameter contract against its body: check whether the stated default activation matches the module actually instantiated, whether a named reduction factor implies division rather than multiplication of the channel count, and whether a dimensionality flag selects the matching convolution type. Explicit inline defect markers or docstring-code contradictions identify the enclosing function as the defect site.

When a composing wrapper forwards a configuration flag into submodules, search for every forwarding site of that class/flag; a propagation defect can live in the caller even when the callee's own branch logic is correct. Distinguish local computation/ordering defects from boundary mis-propagation across wrappers.

Read the existing test to extract the execution contract: which layers are exercised, with which flag values, and what equality is asserted. A forward failure on a lower-dimensional input points to a dimensionality mismatch (the wrong convolution type applied to the tensor rank) rather than a numeric issue, tracing back to the constructor that chose the convolution type or forwarded the flag.

Check the intended block ordering and gating behavior: the sequence should squeeze then excite, and the final activation should gate rather than pass through the same activation used in the bottleneck. Reversed submodule order or a non-gating final activation contradicts the module's declared purpose; tests asserting only output shape will not validate activation identity or ordering, so verify those against the source contract.
skill.trigger: Use when a configurable module or its composing wrapper builds submodules from flags/parameters, and the documented defaults, parameter semantics, or block ordering appear inconsistent with the instantiated operations.

skill.title: Shared-context representation contract mismatch in a parsing helper
knowledge: When a parsing helper splits a shared context key into parts but its caller consumes a structured tuple, enumerate every read and write of that key and read the producing site to determine the stored object type. If the sole producer stores a raw structured value with no normalization or stringification, treat the helper's string-parsing branch as the anomaly and rank the helper first; if a producer or fixture supplies the expected string form, the helper is exonerated and the producer becomes primary.

Before accepting a missing-value repro, check the helper's key-absent default and the producer's assignment/clearing timing. When absence already returns the expected default, the symptom must arise from a key that is present, so inspect inputs that set the key as the observable contract and keep the consuming helper ranked above the producer.

Verify shape claims in comments, docstrings, and callers against the actual data path: a helper whose docstring or return contract promises a tuple while its input parsing assumes a string is a strong shape-mismatch signal, especially when the caller compares the result to a structured literal.

Consider a reused per-document or per-buffer context dictionary: if one context is initialized once and reused across tokens, a stale or wrongly-shaped stored value can survive. When the failing input does not set the key, rank the producer or clear path first and inspect storage timing.
skill.trigger: When localization centers on a helper that parses a shared context or dictionary key, and its producer or consumer appears to disagree about whether the stored value is a string, structured tuple, or other normalized form, especially with a missing-key default branch.

skill.title: Truncated container rewrite with hard-coded replacement leaves embedded declarations stranded
knowledge: When a rewrite routine promises to replace an outer declaration while preserving declarations embedded in its internal subset, read the pattern's excluded character class and the order of operations. If the pattern cannot cross a delimiter that also appears inside the subset, the match is expected to stop at the first inner delimiter; check whether embedded declarations are stripped before the outer match, and treat a missing pre-strip plus a fixed-delimiter pattern as the primary suspect.

Inspect the substitution argument: if the replacement is a constant or generic value rather than reconstructed from the matched text, the rewrite can only replace the truncated fragment and will leave the remaining declarations and closing subset syntax behind. That literal substitution is a high-value discriminator because it explains malformed-output and lost-declaration symptoms without invoking the consumers.

Trace the call site and consumers to separate producer from consumer. If downstream code only stores or expands the routine's returned extracted-declaration mapping and contains no outer-declaration parsing logic, rank the producer's rewrite body higher than the consumer for the reported declaration or entity failure.

Grep for the feature token in tests before fixing a routine; a repository contract that exercises a populated internal subset states the intended behavior. If the production pattern or comment documents only an empty subset example, that contrast indicates the routine was written for the empty case and is the likely defect; use the contract's expected return assertions to confirm responsibility lies with the producer, not the expansion path.
skill.trigger: Applying when a sanitization or serialization rewrite promises to replace an outer declaration/container while preserving declarations embedded in its internal subset, and the observed symptoms include a generic replacement, a truncated match, stray embedded-declaration syntax, or valid input reported as malformed.

skill.title: Asymmetric tie-branch in nested backtracking reconstructor drops equal-score candidates
knowledge: When equal-length candidates are missing from a DP reconstructor, compare the nested backtracking helper's symmetric predecessor branches; candidate accumulation on one tie branch paired with a no-op on the mirror branch is the observable defect signature.

After reading a container method that defines an inner callable, check whether the suspect line number falls between the inner definition line and the end of its body; if so, search the file for the inner callable's name and rank that nested function as its own candidate ahead of the enclosing method and unrelated utilities.

Treat a class-level symbol hit spanning many methods as a coarse pointer, not the candidate granularity: enumerate contained definitions so the smallest callable range bracketing the failing branch can be ranked before broader helpers.

When the bug is in a nested reconstructor, use the enclosing method and unrelated utilities only as fallback candidates; the inner helper's line range bracketing the asymmetric branch establishes responsibility over downstream reporters or DP-table setup.
skill.trigger: A dynamic-programming sequence-alignment reconstructor returns fewer equally scored candidates than expected, and a suspect mismatch or tie branch lies inside a nested helper rather than at the enclosing method's top level.

skill.title: Dispatched selector handler drops the built accumulator and calls an undefined condition builder
knowledge: When a selector handler yields no elements or None, read the handler for that exact selector together with its sibling handlers in the same file: a `return None` where every working sibling ends by returning the built expression/accumulator is the anomaly, because the caller passes the handler's return value straight into the query engine, so a non-returned accumulator breaks selection. If the shared condition builder's body is intact and a sibling uses it correctly, localize to the specific failing handler; redirect to the shared builder only when its body is itself malformed.

Take the condition-builder helper name called inside the failing handler and grep it repo-wide; if the only occurrence is the call site itself, the helper is undefined and the branch cannot produce a condition. Use the sibling handler's call to the real shared builder (e.g., the same builder invoked with the opposite polarity argument) as ground truth for the intended call, then confirm the failing handler's call names that builder.

Read the test covering the failing selector before ranking candidates and use its membership assertions as a discriminator: an explicit expected element set plus a count distinguishes a None return (membership fails immediately) from a swapped condition (wrong membership) from a broken shared builder (only special-case nested elements mishandled while the plain attribute still matches), which rules responsibility in or out for the specific handler versus the shared builder.
skill.trigger: A pseudo-class or name-dispatched selector handler yields no elements or None; the handler is expected to mutate/build a query or expression object that the caller consumes as its return value.

skill.title: CLI path-discovery branch silently drops missing input
knowledge: When a CLI silently ignores an explicitly supplied path, open the generator that expands path arguments and enumerate its per-argument-kind branches (stdin sentinel, regular file, directory, otherwise). A terminal branch that only logs or returns without yielding/dropping the argument into the result set discards it before any downstream checker can see it; if all other branches yield, rank the non-yielding branch as the defect location.

Read the caller that collects the path-discovery results and the per-path consumer/checker. If the checker already maps a propagated missing path or OSError to the expected diagnostic and failure status, the missing yield in discovery is the cause; if the consumer filters or silently skips paths, investigate there instead.

Read the unit tests that import the suspect discovery unit and locate the test for the failing argument kind. An assertion that the generator returns the explicitly supplied missing path is an executable contract on discovery; it cannot pass by only making a warning visible or changing exit-code computation. Use downstream integration expectations for the diagnostic code and exit status to confirm that restoring propagation is sufficient.

When the symptom says 'silently', separate the missing message from the missing process outcome. Check logging configuration for default-verbosity suppression only as a confound; a warning-only branch that yields no path leaves downstream result counts and exit status unchanged, so it cannot satisfy the reported zero-exit failure or a unit-test path-return contract. Choose propagation over logging visibility when the missing input must affect the checker outcome.
skill.trigger: Use when a CLI silently ignores an explicitly provided path argument, usually a non-existent file, and exits successfully even though the per-path checker or error-reporting layer would report a missing-file diagnostic if the path reached it.

skill.title: Row-assembly separator predicates non-exclusive across table shapes
knowledge: When a table-like row assembler emits structural separator lines, grep the package for the separator literal and eliminate unrelated producers such as horizontal-rule handling. If the surviving sites are the row assembler's own branches, rank that converter first and treat table wrappers and cell converters as producers of content only.

For every separator-emission branch in the row assembler, record its parent/section predicate and evaluate it for each fixture shape: header plus body, body only, plain rows without section tags, and caption or colspan cases. Non-exclusive predicates yield duplicate separators, while predicates keyed only on parent tag miss body-only or plain shapes; the expected invariant is usually one separator immediately after whichever row is emitted first.

Read the table tests as a contract before choosing between the row assembler and the cell converters: extract one asserted literal per structural shape and ask whether separator count and placement are keyed to parent tag or to emitted row order. Uniform expectations across header, body-only, plain, and caption fixtures falsify any parent-tag-keyed rule, narrowing the fault to separator placement or duplication in the row assembler while cell converter outputs remain consistent apart from their content.

Inside the row assembler, verify first-row detection and separator width locally: check whether the first-row predicate uses a descendant accessor that can also match nested rows, and whether width is derived by counting delimiters in already-assembled text rather than from header-cell count. Distinguish a wrong predicate from the wrong pairing of a header-append branch with a body-prepend branch, keeping the row assembler ranked either way.
skill.trigger: HTML-to-Markdown table conversion emits duplicated, missing, or misplaced header/body separator rows, and a row-assembly converter is responsible for inserting those separators; use before ranking cell converters or table wrappers.

skill.title: Rendering function calls undefined instance helper with orphaned module imports
knowledge: For each action or page-rendering function you read, list every `self.<name>(` call and grep `def <name>` across the repo; a call that has no definition anywhere marks that function as the rewritten anomaly, so rank it first even when the issue keywords name a different feature.

Back the missing-helper finding with a dead-dependency check: grep the module's imports and module-level caches; if they are now referenced nowhere else in the module, the function that used to consume them was replaced, confirming the same candidate.

Read the test that covers a suspicious candidate before ranking it: a test asserting the suspicious behavior (especially with a defect/TODO comment) treats that behavior as contracted pre-existing behavior, so do not blame it for the injected regression; redirect to functions whose behavior the tests do not describe.
If grep instead resolves the called helper to an actual definition, the call is benign and you should shift suspicion back to the caller's arguments or the state it builds.
skill.trigger: Issue text points at a downstream feature output (feed/serialization/metadata) being incomplete or malformed, while an action or page-rendering function's body contains self.<helper>(...) calls with no matching definition and its module-level imports/caches are no longer referenced anywhere.

fault_subtype: action function rewritten to call an undefined instance helper while orphaning module-level imports and caches

skill.title: Rendering function calls undefined instance helper with orphaned module imports
knowledge: For each action or page-rendering function you read, list every `self.<name>(` call and grep `def <name>` across the repo; a call that has no definition anywhere marks that function as the rewritten anomaly, so rank it first even when the issue keywords name a different feature.

Back the missing-helper finding with a dead-dependency check: grep the module's imports and module-level caches; if they are now referenced nowhere else in the module, the function that used to consume them was replaced, confirming the same candidate.

Read the test that covers a suspicious candidate before ranking it: a test asserting the suspicious behavior (especially with a defect/TODO comment) treats that behavior as contracted pre-existing behavior, so do not blame it for the injected regression; redirect to functions whose behavior the tests do not describe.
If grep instead resolves the called helper to an actual definition, the call is benign and you should shift suspicion back to the caller's arguments or the state it builds.
skill.trigger: Issue text points at a downstream feature output (feed/serialization/metadata) being incomplete or malformed, while an action or page-rendering function's body contains self.<helper>(...) calls with no matching definition and its module-level imports/caches are no longer referenced anywhere.

skill.title: Rendering function calls undefined instance helper with orphaned module imports
knowledge: When a function on a suspected issue path calls a helper whose definition is unclear, inspect the receiver's class, bases, and dynamic attribute providers. If the helper remains unresolved, trace whether the call can execute under the reported conditions and affect the reported output before increasing the caller's priority.

Unused imports or caches can suggest that an implementation path changed. Use them to identify dependencies and call sites worth inspecting, then check how those components participate in the reported behavior; keep missing use as a hypothesis until that connection is supported.

Compare a suspicious candidate's behavior with callers, existing test assertions, and the issue's expected result. A test or TODO documents an expectation or known concern to investigate; when they disagree with the issue, establish whether the reported execution follows that path before retaining or excluding the candidate.
